name: Tobias Read
subject: “Oregon’s secretary of state makes case for drop-box voting.”
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
I was just in Philomath this weekend, sitting in a small town hall with neighbors asking honest questions about something that should never be controversial: how they can trust that their vote will be counted.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
Here’s what I told them — and what I need you to hear too.
Oregon’s elections are secure, accurate, and built to work for real life. Vote-by-mail works. Drop boxes work. And people across our state rely on both to make their voices heard.
But right now, those systems are under pressure from every direction.
Just this week, Oregon joined other states in court to block yet another unconstitutional attempt to interfere with how Americans vote. We’ve already beat these attacks before — and we intend to do it again.
But defending our elections isn’t just happening in courtrooms. It’s happening in every county, every clerk’s office, and every community where voters are deciding how to return their ballots.
This work takes vigilance. It takes resources. And it takes a public willing to stand up for a simple idea: that democracy belongs to the people who live here—not to politicians trying to rewrite the rules from the top down.
We’re going to keep strengthening our elections. And we’re going to keep making sure every eligible Oregonian can cast a ballot safely and confidently.
If you’re with me in this fight to protect voting rights in Oregon, I’m asking you to pitch in today. Your support helps us communicate directly with Oregonians and defend vote-by-mail, secure our elections, and push back against dangerous attempts to make it harder for people to vote. body:
Today, we’re asking for you to split a donation between the Kentucky Democratic Senate Nominee Fund and our grassroots movement »
#
Peter,
Kentucky hasn't sent a Democrat to the U.S. Senate in over thirty years.
**But this year, we have a real opportunity to take Kentucky’s U.S. Senate seat back for working families — and we need your help to do it.** Here’s the situation:
Mitch McConnell — who’s held this seat for more than four decades — has finally announced his intent to retire. For the first time in a generation, that seat is up for grabs.
Now here’s what makes this moment so remarkable... _Kentucky has one of the most popular Democratic governors in America._ Andy Beshear has proven that a candidate with the right message and proven results can win working people's trust. And Democrats have a real shot at doing it again — this time, for an open U.S. Senate seat.

body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]
Friends,
Consumers must be in the driver’s seat when it comes to data privacy. California has laws on the books to protect your personal data, and as Attorney General, I’ll always go to bat for you when companies break those laws and trample your rights.
I’m proud to announce that we’ve secured a $12.75 million settlement against General Motors for illegally retaining and selling Californians’ location and driving data to data brokers.
If that’s all you need to hear, please click here to support these fights and ensure I can keep fighting on your behalf. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26?amount=50]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26?amount=50]
Here's what GM was doing: Through OnStar (the service that provides directions and emergency roadside assistance), GM collected precise location data and detailed driving behavior from hundreds of thousands of California drivers, as well as from drivers across the nation.
Then, from 2020 to 2024, GM secretly sold that data to data brokers without their customers’ knowledge or consent, and despite explicitly telling customers it would never do so.
GM reportedly made approximately $20 million nationwide from these sales — and the data brokers? They intended to market this data to insurance companies to help set customers’ rates.
All the while, GM was telling customers in its own privacy policy that it did not sell driving or location data, and if it did disclose data for insurance purposes, it’d be with consumers’ express consent.
What happened is illegal, plain and simple — and today we’re holding GM accountable.
Today’s settlement requires that the company pay $12.75 million in civil penalties, abandon these illegal practices, delete driving data within 180 days, and build a real privacy program subject to ongoing oversight.
This is also the first time we've enforced California's data minimization principle — the common sense rule that companies can't just stockpile your data and use it later for purposes you never agreed to.
We’re sending a message to corporate America: If you illegally collect, store, or sell consumer data, we won’t hesitate to hold you accountable.
California's privacy laws are the strongest in the nation — and we intend to keep enforcing them, no matter how big the company. If you’re with me in this fight, I’m asking you to join my re-election campaign and chip in to help power our fights ahead. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26?amount=50]

Hi Peter, I’m going to be upfront. This is another fundraising email.

I know, I know... but if you’ll give me a minute of your time, I’ll explain
why [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260511-1-ak.NE6rHq&amount=10&refcode=em20260511-2140&t=1004&akid=2141%2E251025%2ECsJBbe ]your donation today would make a huge difference in stopping Donald
Trump and the disease in our politics that led to him. (More on that
below.)

Still here? Thank you. It means a lot. 🙏

A while ago, I said something that people weren’t quite ready to hear:
Donald Trump is not the disease. He’s just the worst symptom of the
disease.

I know that sounds like a bumper sticker, so let me explain what I mean.

Our current political system isn’t designed to help working people. Just
look at healthcare, for example.

Corporate PAC donations from insurance companies have flowed into various
campaigns, and as a result:

* Bought-out politicians tell us something like Medicare for All is an
“impossible” feat.
* Big Pharma continues to raise prices and squeeze working people.
* No real change comes from our government year after year.

And that’s just one of the many ways corporations and MAGA billionaires
have rigged our political system in their favor.

Back to Trump.

Trump didn't build that rot. He just knew how to exploit it — and the
truth is, when Trump is eventually gone, the rot will still be there.

Unless we elect people who refuse to play that game.

That's why I dropped everything to run. I've seen the pain the broken
system causes, up close, and I know how to fight it.

When I was Director of Wayne County's Department of Health, Human and
Veteran Services, we spearheaded a program to erase $700 million in
medical debt for 300,000 Michiganders.

Peter, just
imagine what we could accomplish from a Senate seat.

I can promise you this: I won't send strongly-worded letters and call that
fighting back against Trump. I'll use every tool at my disposal — every
bit of power, every platform, every ounce of what I know about how this
system works — to fight for working people.

But none of that matters if we lose.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260511-1-ak.NE6rHq&amount=10&refcode=em20260511-2140&t=1005&akid=2141%2E251025%2ECsJBbe ]That’s why I’m humbly asking for your donation today. We’re narrowly
leading in the polls, and with less than three months until our August
primary election, this is the time to pitch in and help us win. Can I
count on your support,
Peter?

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260511-1-ak.NE6rHq&amount=10&refcode=em20260511-2140&t=1024&akid=2141%2E251025%2ECsJBbe ]Donate $10 ››

In solidarity,

Abdul

clean_body: This is what they fear most | Friend, After weeks of watching Marsha Blackburn and her Republican cronies in the Tennessee state legislature rig voter district maps in an attempt to silence voters, we think it's important to share something that’s been overlooked. There is STILL a very real reason to keep hope alive. The same day the GOP called their special session to vote on the new maps, county primaries were already happening across Tennessee in all but nine counties. And the numbers told a very different story about the will of the voters than the one Republicans want you to believe. Democrats are turning out in HUGE numbers. In Shelby County, and in particular, across the suburbs, voters are energized, engaged, and ready to fight back. Democratic turnout increased by over 65%. So, while Republicans would like you to believe that the November election is a foregone conclusion, Tennesseans are proving otherwise at the ballot box. In county after county, Democratic turnout was up, a trend that Republicans would rather not talk about. In Williamson County alone (Marsha Blackburn’s home county), Democratic turnout was up by over 600 percent. The energy is real. The momentum is growing. And unlike Tennessee Republicans, the numbers don’t lie. People are paying attention to what’s happening in our state. They’re tired of political games.They’re tired of attacks on our rights and our communities. And they’re showing up because they know Tennessee deserves better leadership. But turnout alone won’t change this state. We have to keep organizing. We have to keep engaging voters. We have to keep turning people out to vote in August and again in November with everything we’ve got. If we do that, if we stay united and keep building this movement block by block, neighborhood by neighborhood, we will flip seats in races people said were impossible, and shock the country in the process. Republicans want you to believe your voice doesn’t matter.Don’t give them that victory. Your vote matters a lot. If it didn’t, they wouldn't be working so hard to silence it. Your organizing matters. Your energy matters. If you’re ready to help us keep this momentum going,= | | = And together , we can win. Thank you, Alex Hensley Campaign Manager Jerri Green for Tennessee Governor P.S. clean_body: I've enclosed our latest campaign update on the status of this critical runoff election. Please Read: | MESSAGE FROM CHIP ROY Let me be direct. Nearly two million Texans turned out in the Republican Primary for Attorney General—and despite being massively outspent and targeted by the political establishment and their wealthy backers, we forced this race into a runoff. That didn't happen by accident. It happened because the people of Texas still value truth over spin—and results over a bankroll. My opponent poured more than $16 million of his own money into this race, only to finish at 39%. Meanwhile, we were hit by a California-based, left-wing PAC angry that I stood with Donald Trump to strip out hundreds of billions in Green New Deal-style subsidies from the so-called "Big Beautiful Bill." They thought they could buy Texas.They were wrong. The runoff election is May 26 - less than three weeks away - and with your help, we're going to finish what we started and prove, once again, that Texas isn't for sale. But let's be honest about what's at stake. This is no time to hand the Attorney General's office to someone who's never set foot in a courtroom. Texas is facing serious challenges: a wide-open border, foreign adversaries buying up our land, and a radical agenda determined to reshape our state and our country. We need a proven conservative who knows how to fight - and win. The Attorney General isn't a ceremonial role. It's the chief legal officer of the largest conservative state in America. It requires leadership from day one—building a strong legal team, enforcing the law without hesitation, and taking the fight wherever it's needed to defend Texas. I'm ready to do that. But I need to know if conservatives like you are in this fight with me. ## Derby Bob’s 80th Straight Kentucky Derby
Bob Weihe first attended the Kentucky Derby in 1947, when his mother took him at age 9 and told him to crawl through the crowd to catch a glimpse of the horses. He hasn't missed one since. On Saturday, May 2, the 89-year-old Louisville man—after four months in the hospital and a recent stay in hospice care—[made it to his 80th](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJys0D2u3CAUxfHV4I4RXH9OQZGG7qVNiTBcbPIYQIAHeffRZA2vPtLRT_8_X-pL--Dj8Vu_ULjDqeaSithrwNawqOjNtev9LtiuEqs2OjftY3UKGCyUzZRzlUuqGU1T02CFQwQcBxR8Xbd5ZCuH4RSAbAJYt5Ezs8wW50lbPo-rNsxohzB48TlkM-fA-AbPB5pxedpNW3BPt-4rmRha31J5_E0-thNduNMby8Ok1xDE2VquZPxFQBKQvfcH1hw_IwF5plKRFm18PAjI2lK5CUhFQHpLQE7bMq3TxAnIb4ztMt83tVj2m5rzKub0IVCbeqy0FZ8DUlNSj3RPO-3oT6RHChYjbfjKaSjC5u5D8HX5qI-X9uG_sv1E4beAfwEAAP__sWqVEg). His family wasn't sure it would happen. Bob's blood pressure had been nosediving for months, and he couldn't eat. Then in mid-April, his reading came back a perfect 120/80. He told his family he wanted to go home, and from there, he set his sights on the Derby. Churchill Downs provided tickets after a [CBS reporter's public plea](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskL2OvCAUxZ9GOwwgfhUU_8Zu_u2W5gqXkR0EA3fG-PYb9xm2O8lJzsfv67E8wAcfn_9hR-2ebiGXlohnCUiEeYnevFdYr4z0zrGAgYPAx-IWyWXPeMeEWI6cyoGGFlVb7RAltjVqMQxj1_JByHrTXHWqVwZAWHCdmoxwkzXroPpxbRU3tdd3IO-EkFyMcmrQtP1kR7DSTW5Yh0pxtJ5Sbr6Tj7ShC1f6YG5M2uugN6KjVO2_Ss6VnM_zbMxa7iO3X8n5lpWcx4ldCJmlYNkOkfnItlQOb5ABEUZb2Asjvc3rYhbzelVyrrO2x-lD8KW_Zzx38OG3lv4C2UfLnwAAAP__22mFQQ), and Bob arrived with a police escort, wearing a custom hat reading "Derby Bob's 80th." He was welcomed as a VIP, met the track president, and watched Golden Tempo rally from last to win in a historic race, the [first Derby victory for a female trainer](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJys0DGO6yAYBODT2J0twAFMQfEad3ntlgjDT8wGgwV_Evn2K-8Ztp-ZT5qvu7nbmGJ-_Lc76PAIBkMxGT4tASJUk6N7rXY9K-Cr5madPdDG3IJhhImB8IFSc9TSDnBobr3XAYDB1IOmUs58IpKyftNBBakcBcH5xKkKSomwSipU4MGuE-2jvgYJp5QROjM1gpuE8rP17OqusrsR8BFLHb9LzLhBSGd5Qx1d2fukN8SjddO_ji0dW9pRKrbxtFspV6Bji60YXYLWsWVWQ0l-eELGl3ueg4e6nkOweaCSkhvjQo0b7qmv2h-fmFJs4vIfu43p18O_-Oqt2U8AAAD__4vBgTs). He even picked the three horses that finished in the top three, netting a family member around $56,000. Back home that night, surrounded by a dozen family members, Bob summed it up: "I'm still alive."
## Former NICU Baby Gives Back
Abigail Williford was born 10 weeks early, weighing just 2 pounds, 11 ounces. She spent her [first 91 days in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskEGupCAQQE-juzJCd4suWMymd3-2szSFFMIEwUCp8faT_pkj_Au8vPf-fM1fGGJI62_cSLvVzezynOiqkZipzCksh0FzF-KjpIoL7owhVTfLXg7Qv0CIeS-57rTw_GytdkSSHi1podT4evRKyNbrwaLAl7OTEdKqEceeDE32qQZJ6mlMG_QH2L-EkL0Y5dTR8hgmO6KVbnLKqObZkw2cS_c3h8SeXLzzSaVb8tZG7Zn32jx-NfLdyPd1XR0thyeM7Ltc1ka-zxyPxEQJ0JgbrhBjcLlY-N8GmNKBMd7AGdgTbHgnLBYWH6ItlCr4XPfAGOGzBdgjQ8WTLHgqEIOjRr7bou3-Da_DR3rdMMRvSf6JwaeW_wIAAP__cgaYlA) at James and Connie Maynard Children's Hospital in North Carolina. Every year since, her family has returned on her birthday with a cake to celebrate with the staff who cared for her. Now 18 and a senior at the North Carolina School of Science and Mathematics, Abby has also logged more than [75 hours of volunteer work](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskL1uhDAQhJ8GOp-wzZ8LF2muu7Qp0QJr2MTYlr3H6d4-Is-QcjTS6Jvv6zE9gDyF7RMOtG5zE7s4BXwVj8yYp0DLc4b5nZGfORRYIDFQKG5SjepF0wkpp5RjSbjw1NardYgKdY1WDsPY6WaQqt6tNKYF1xsYpNTjDLrrVQcrmFYbdCBrstdg00mpGjkqc8NF92YdYVXOuGEeqrbBlTjm23ekwDs6_44n5tsSj9rbnTmVSn9U6l6pe8KYPF5Vpe4u5gOzuK6IBEwYWCwxMIUnhU1wFBudKGZYfq7AOwpGOMRrj6LAiavYMQspTa-NUXW2a3qR91T6C2o7gPwfBP-HwNOq3wAAAP__-KSJnA) at the hospital, rotating through departments from the emergency room to the cancer center. "_I know some babies born premature like I was don't make it to 18, especially 18 and healthy,_ " she said. "_I think that's an amazing accomplishment and testament to both my doctors and God_." This fall, Abby will begin studying biology and public health at [East Carolina University Honors College](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJys0D3u3CAUBPDT2B0WPPwBBUUad5s2JcLwsIkwWMCutbePnDP865F-o5k_L_0yIYa0_zYnKr973XzWCe8asTUsOgX73sz2LdjeJVVjzdVMSNVroDATOhHG9FVyvdA2PfZOeURA3qNiyyImThcG_aGoHCfL5o2D9cAYpeMmBZ834GK2I536oB6QTowBZQLkgJbP0gnjwEu_bEs3UnSh5TL8zSG1A3385g-Wweazj-po7aod_9XB2sF63_dgcnyyDlZTWrARawerQ2scVlIvTC6knUhGnPlW8gwlTFDJFpjEcLQz9kW56w4xhjo_9ftpwn-ybz9x1UfBvwAAAP__5pF_pQ) on a pre-med track, with plans to become a physician. Her mother, Kimberly, said the NICU experience planted the seed early. "_We are forever grateful for the hands that held our daughter at the very beginning. Because of them, we get to watch her step into a future that once felt uncertain_."
## Dog Rescued from 13th-Floor Ledge
A Jack Russell terrier named Elbie was [rescued from a 13th-floor ledge](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskD1uhDAQRk9jOiPPsPwVLtLQbdqUyOAxOAIb2bOLyOkjcoZ0X_X0vvf1HJ_Gbz4sn2Yn7RY3sotjoDNvxExpDH5-TWa6EvErhWxmc7DxIbsRFTZS1RJgPFLMB808PgqrHRFSVZCGtu3qSrWAxaqp7hpsqVHTBA4BTO8mYw06qKCzExRe30BVA6CCDvuS5qrpbWcsut61UyseiqznmMrv6AOv5LYrvimVc9yLTa_MRxbVh8BB4HCeZwn3jXKOZfgRONx0gYN63LsTONi4yER5fpGVLsVdQsWrzBwTXTI6mS8b6JKrX1aZfCZpHFOSfEZpzZUFDkXS9jj9tvnc3HrLbvz2p8P_kfKt8TcAAP__HxWLbQ) of a Sydney high-rise after spending two days stranded. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. subject: Ward 3 PVD News

body:
| |
---
Hello Friends & Neighbors,

With the return of the Lippitt Park Farmers Market, we know that spring has finally sprung! This is one of my favorite times of year in the neighborhood — as everyone re-emerges after a long winter, looking to spend time connecting with neighbors in parks and neighborhoods!

| You can always find my newsletters at **[https://www.sueanderbois.com/news](https://sue4ri.com/l/oqJWZSLZq7fo)** | | [ **CHECK IT OUT** ](https://sue4ri.com/l/7EQl1wWWeVe5)
---
**[Or have anything you want me to know? Share here>>](https://sue4ri.com/l/9Y7uN5K82HI0)**
| [ **SHARE YOUR THOUGHTS** ](https://sue4ri.com/l/3HGQIGsihgOB)
---

As always, there’s a lot to share — so I’ll hop right into it!

Sue

| **Green Revolving Fund Passes Out Of Committee** As you remember, two years ago, I wrote and passed a law requiring all municipal buildings to be carbon neutral by 2040. The City’s Sustainability Department has been hard at work on implementation — and just released the Decarbonization Roadmap! As part of implementation, I am partnering with the Administration to create a Green Revolving Fund, so we can reinvest the savings from energy efficiency and clean energy upgrades — and any incentives we receive — into future projects.

With so much building and renovating underway and so many attacks on clean energy from the federal government, it was important to move quickly — and my Special Committee on the Environment and Resiliency passed the ordinance out of Committee on Friday, May 1st. The full Council will now vote on it on May 7th and 21st.

**[You can read about the ordinance in the Providence Business News!](https://sue4ri.com/l/BP2kx0IJjQSI)** | | [ **READ MORE** ](https://sue4ri.com/l/cCpQznQkcVVe)
---

**Upcoming Events** **Ward 3 Community Meeting:** **The next meeting is on May 16th at 10 a.m. at the Mount Hope Community Center!** We will have several special guests: City Traffic Engineer Nate Urso to discuss traffic calming on Hope Street; Director of Real Estate Nick Ciccitelli to discuss the sale of the Rochambeau Fire Station, and School Board Chairman Ty’relle Stephens. As always, we’ll have plenty of time for conversation & questions! **Budget Review:** This year’s budget is being thoroughly vetted by the “Ways and Means Committee”, of which I am a member. As we have done in prior years on the Finance Committee, the Committee will meet at least 2x a week through mid-June to review each department’s budget, and we will have a second public hearing once the Council’s proposed amended budget is available for feedback. Please feel welcome to send me feedback at any time, and you can see the updated meeting schedule on the **[City’s open meetings portal.](https://sue4ri.com/l/17i5ADIBoKrN)** We will also be posting regular updates to the calendar on the **[Council’s Facebook Page](https://sue4ri.com/l/DniXONMplaUm)** to ensure folks can engage! **North Burial Ground Master Plan Community Visioning Session** North Burial Ground is developing a Master Plan to guide the cemetery for both short-term improvements and the long-term development and maintenance of NBG.

Join us on June 1, 5:30-7:30 PM at Roger Williams Park, Clark Dalrymple Boathouse, 1000 Elmwood Ave, Providence RI 02907.

RSVP to**aheppner@providenceri.gov** by Thursday, May 28. **Miscellaneous:** **May 30th: Porchfest!** I am so excited for the East Side’s annual music festival! Keep up with the latest updates and the lineup of performances through **[Porchfest’s social media.](https://sue4ri.com/l/2o0ht98Q95Xy)**
---

**Miscellaneous Topics For You** **North Main Street:** Work continues with our North Main Street Task Force! The City is currently working through the contracting for the firm that will undertake the design/engineering phase of the larger changes to North Main! I can’t wait to announce who the selected contractor is.

We are also working on two minor zone changes on North Main so that existing properties can add some units of housing and mixed-use development! As soon as there are plans to share, I will share them — but I am so excited for what’s in store! **Flock Cameras:** A big thank you to RIC Professor Robyn Linde (and Ward 3 resident!) and her class who did an excellent semester project investigating Flock cameras and their potential impacts on our rights to privacy. The Flock contract is not currently up for renegotiation in Providence, but will be in a year, so it’s important for my colleagues and me to understand the implications of this system. I have had serious concerns about Flock’s relationship with ICE, and while Providence itself has rules in place to not share data with ICE — it is important to understand how ICE has been able to access data in other places and use it to infringe on personal freedoms of residents. The class presented to my Special Committee, and materials will be posted here. **Newsmakers Segment:** Did you check out my segment on Newsmakers last week? **[See it here!](https://sue4ri.com/l/CuWj2JFgEjTc)** | | [ **CHECK IT OUT** ](https://sue4ri.com/l/KENBUDPI92fS)
---

**Follow My Socials For Live Updates!** Between newsletters, I post frequent updates on more time-sensitive matters and general updates on what’s going on in council. You can follow below to make sure you don’t miss a thing! | [](https://sue4ri.com/l/sxUYVtOGmOZ6) | [](https://sue4ri.com/l/wTO5OxqCLWWF) | [](https://sue4ri.com/l/YuL9PzaQiaNx)
---|---|---

It continues to be my greatest honor to serve our community on the Providence City Council.

Please reach out any time by replying to this email if there are issues of importance to you or ways I can be of service to you. Budget season is a busy season at City Hall, so thank you in advance for your patience if my email inbox gets a little flooded, and I take a day or two to respond — I do try to reply individually to every (non-form) email I receive!

With Gratitude,

Sue A
---
|
* * *
**** This communications is on behalf of Sue AnderBois' City Council work ****

Councilor Sue AnderBois represents Ward 3, which includes the Mount Hope, Hope Village (Summit), Collyer Park, and Blackstone neighborhoods. She currently serves as the Deputy Majority Whip and the Chair of the North Main Street Task Force and the Special Committee on Environment and Resiliency. She is also a member of the Committee on Finance, Committee on City Property, Special Committee on Health, Opportunity, Prosperity, and Education (HOPE), and is a member of the Board of Parks Commissioners.

Her career has been focused on public policy solutions for climate change, clean energy, and sustainable food systems.
---
| Paid for by Friends of AnderBois
---

166 5th St, PVD 02906

Team, In the midst of campaign craziness, it is important to take time to remember the origin story: why did Seth first choose to serve in our politics over a decade ago? In the video below, Seth's friends and family sit down and talk about who he is, why he keeps choosing the hard path, and what drives him to keep fighting. It's a few minutes long, but we think it's worth your time. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131209437/620305059/2090747700?refcode=260511_sfm_mm1_img&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS83NDc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1ZjIyNzgyNi03OTRkLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ZSnYTZiQXKy-OZLcUiNLQ3CNIwa1Yqh7oR-MT7MwM7U=) Seth graduated from college three months before 9/11. He didn't know there was going to be a war, but he joined the Marines because he didn't want someone else to have to go in his place. After four tours in Iraq, he took on an entrenched incumbent as his first ever foray into politics. He won and has served to represent the sixth district of Massachusetts for the last ten years. Now, he’s once again challenging a fifty-year incumbent, doing so again because we can't afford to wait another six years for meaningful change. This goes a long way towards confirming what we already knew. Just last week, Mark was back in court defending his free speech rights from Hegseth’s baseless attacks. And now, only a few days later, Hegseth is directing a new Pentagon review of Mark for speaking out.

My family's story starts in Alabama — where Jim Crow made it almost impossible for Black families to vote, be heard, or build political power. Like so many others, they came north to Detroit seeking opportunity and a real voice in our democracy. The Voting Rights Act helped make that promise real. It protected communities from being carved up and silenced. It made full Black political participation possible in America. **Last month’s Supreme Court ruling in Louisiana v. Callais puts all of that at risk. ** The Court’s decision opens the door to MAGA gerrymandering on a scale that could decide control of Congress before a single vote is cast. It's part of a broader plan to rig the system so it works only for them — not for the people. I think about my family when I hear that. And I think about what's at stake if we don't fight back. I’m 6'8"— I was made to Stand TALL. As Michigan's Secretary of State, I will use every tool available to protect Michigan voters and defend our democracy. It’s up to all of us to pitch in to protect, restore, and expand voting rights. Our grandparents won them in 1965. We must reclaim them in 2026 by winning Secretary of State races in swing states like Michigan and everywhere in America. clean_body: | = = Hi friend — I'm Garlin Gilchrist, Lieutenant Governor and the Democratic candidate for Secretary of State in Michigan. My family's story starts in Alabama — where Jim Crow made it almost impossible for Black families to vote, be heard, or build political power. Like so many others, they came north to Detroit seeking opportunity and a real voice in our democracy. The Voting Rights Act helped make that promise real. It protected communities from being carved up and silenced. It made full Black political participation possible in America. Last month’s Supreme Court ruling in Louisiana v. Callais puts all of that at risk. The Court’s decision opens the door to MAGA gerrymandering on a scale that could decide control of Congress before a single vote is cast. It's part of a broader plan to rig the system so it works only for them — not for the people. I think about my family when I hear that. And I think about what's at stake if we don't fight back. I’m 6'8"— I was made to Stand TALL. As Michigan's Secretary of State, I will use every tool available to protect Michigan voters and defend our democracy. It’s up to all of us to pitch in to protect, restore, and expand voting rights. Our grandparents won them in 1965. We must reclaim them in 2026 by winning Secretary of State races in swing states like Michigan and everywhere in America. If we lose these seats to MAGA extremists, they will consolidate more power and take away more rights from more people. It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 _ _ and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250th birthday. Friend, this Memorial Day marks the first major national act of remembrance of the veterans who made the ultimate sacrifice to defend America from its enemies and ensure it has remained the Land of the Free for the last 250 years. And this year's National Memorial Day Parade will be a special edition - the biggest parade yet - where national memory meets living history as veterans from every military generation celebrate America and honor the service and sacrifice of their fallen brethren. Friend, the National Memorial Day Parade is ENIRELY FUNDED by private contributions, including from generous patriots like you. WWII veterans were a key part of the first parade when it was revived in 2005, as they have been every year since for the last 20 years. But this may be the last year we have the opportunity to have these brave men and women with us for the parade. | | | | | | | | This year is a rare moment when living witnesses to World War II and America 's 250th birthday overlap. And no matter how much you can give to this important cause, I want to ask something additional of you. On Memorial Day - not just this momentous year of military milestones, but every year - please join me in honoring those who made the ultimate sacrifice for our freedoms. Come to the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. Visit a local veterans' cemetery. Send a note to a family of the fallen. Or simply take a quiet moment to think about the men and women who gave their lives to defend OUR country. I believe that while we can never do enough to express our gratitude to our defenders, veterans, and first responders, we can always do a little more. Friend, thank you for your support of America 's heroes. Sincerely, Tim Holbert President American Veterans Center | | | The mission of the American Veterans Center and the World War II Veterans Committee is to preserve and promote the legacy and experiences of America's veterans and active duty service personnel from World War II through today. A non-profit educational organization, the AVC and WWIIVC are funded solely through generous contributions from people like you. All contributions are tax-deductible. I’ll be the first to admit, I'm not your typical candidate.
You might actually recognize me from TV — and no, not from a campaign ad.
In December 2023, I walked onto the Jeopardy! Champions Wildcard stage as a Marine Corps Intelligence Officer stationed in Stuttgart, Germany. Heading into Final Jeopardy, I had a lead, a category I liked, and a decision to make.
I bet everything...
... and I was right.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg]
That's how I approach most things in life. You do your homework, you back your judgment, and you don't flinch when the stakes are high.
Right now, the stakes couldn't be higher — and I'm asking you to back me as I take on my next challenge: Running for Congress.
My name is Tyler Vandenberg, and I'm a Democrat running for Congress in California's 6th District. I'm a Harvard Kennedy School graduate, a former Marine officer, and a proud Californian who has spent his career serving this country and our democracy. Now, I’m coming home to fight for it.
Will you chip in $25, $50, or even $100 today to my campaign and Resist Reclaim Rebuild to help us WIN? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg]
DONATE TODAY TO HELP WIN THIS RACE! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg]
I didn't come to this decision lightly. After the 2024 election, I watched MAGA Extremists launch attack after attack on everything I love about this state and this country. Cuts to wildland firefighters. Slashing Medicaid. Threatening to sell off our National Forests. Gutting the agencies that keep our communities safe and our air and water clean.
And then there's Kevin Kiley — my opponent, the man currently occupying this seat.
Kiley has recently tried to rebrand himself as an "independent."
Don't believe it for a second.
Kevin Kiley votes with Donald Trump virtually every single time. The independent label is a costume he's trying on because he knows his record is a liability. He's not independent. He's MAGA with crafty branding.
California's 6th deserves better. And I intend to deliver it.
Here's what I'm going to fight for when I get to Congress:
I'm going to fight to make California affordable again. Housing costs are crushing working families across this district. I'll push for real solutions — more housing supply, stronger tenant protections, and federal investment in the infrastructure that makes communities livable. The cost of living isn't a talking point to me. I worked two restaurant jobs just to make rent when I was starting out. I know what it means to hustle just to get by.
I'm going to fight to protect our public lands and our environment. The GOP wants to sell off our National Forests. I want to protect them, fund them, and keep them accessible to every Californian — not just the wealthy few who can afford what comes after privatization. California's wilderness is not for sale.
I'm going to fight to defend Social Security and Medicare. These aren't government handouts — they're promises this country made to working people. I'll oppose any effort to cut, privatize, or undermine them, full stop.
I'm going to fight to protect our neighbors. Immigrants, women, and LGBTQ+ Californians are under assault from this administration. That ends when we flip this seat.
And I'm going to hold MAGA accountable. Not just with speeches — with votes, with investigations, with every tool available to a Member of Congress. The era of consequence-free MAGA corruption has to end somewhere. It can end here.
I spent years in the Marine Corps learning that servant leadership isn't a slogan — it's a discipline. It means showing up, doing the hard work, and putting the people you serve ahead of yourself. That's the kind of congressman I intend to be.
I'm not coming to Washington to build a brand or further my own career.
I'm coming to do the job.
But I need your help to get there. Races like this one don't flip themselves. They flip because people like you decide early that it's worth fighting for — and put their money where their values are.
So, can I count on you to chip in to my campaign TODAY? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg]
CHIP IN TO HELP DEMS RETAKE THE HOUSE! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg]
Every dollar goes directly toward building the campaign that beats Kevin Kiley and sends California's 6th a representative who actually works for them.
Let's get to work.
— Tyler Vandenberg

**ICYMI: NEW POLL SHOWS JULIA LETLOW HAS COMMANDING LEAD IN U.S. SENATE RACE** _LETLOW DOMINATING THE FIELD WITH A DOUBLE DIGIT LEAD_
**BATON ROUGE, LA** — A new independent [poll](https://us.list-manage.com/13bcqCBoOXY?e=95355a072c&c2id=cd64ea42b1b0eeac0fd7d107db75288a) shows Congresswoman Julia Letlow, the Trump-endorsed candidate for U.S. Senate in Louisiana, continuing to build overwhelming momentum in Louisiana’s Republican U.S. Senate primary, expanding her lead and solidifying her position as the clear frontrunner in the race.
The poll shows **Congresswoman** **Letlow leading the field with 42% support** , compared to D.C. lobbyist John Fleming at 29.6% and Senator Bill Cassidy at 19.6%.
**Quantus Insights’ analysis of the race stated:**

_”The significance is not merely that Letlow leads. It is how the race arrived here. In Quantus’ February 23–24 survey, Fleming stood in front with 34.2%, while Letlow sat at 24.6%. Cassidy was at 19.8%, and more than one in five voters remained undecided. By May, Letlow had climbed roughly seventeen points, Fleming had fallen roughly five, Cassidy had scarcely moved, and the undecided vote had meaningfully compressed. The electorate did not scatter. It sorted.”_
The polling also demonstrates Letlow’s commanding strength in potential runoff matchups. In a head-to-head race against Bill Cassidy, **Letlow leads 63.0% to** 23.4%. Against D.C. lobbyist John Fleming, **Letlow leads 45.4%** to 39.6%.
Among strong MAGA and America First voters, **Letlow holds an even more decisive advantage, leading D.C. lobbyist Fleming by more than 20 points, 52.4% to 31.2%** , underscoring the strength of her support among the conservative base of the Republican electorate.
---
|
---
| | The new numbers mark another major milestone for Letlow’s campaign, which has continued to gain strength across Louisiana as voters rally behind President Trump’s endorsed conservative in the race. The poll also underscores the growing contrast between Letlow’s campaign and Senator Cassidy’s continued collapse with Republican voters.
Since entering the race with President Trump’s complete and total endorsement, Letlow has built a broad coalition of support across Louisiana by focusing on conservative values, support for the America First agenda, protecting parents’ rights, securing the border, strengthening Louisiana’s energy industry, and delivering results for Louisiana families.
To learn more visit [JuliaLetlow.com](https://us.list-manage.com/qiQIxHSEql4?e=95355a072c&c2id=cd64ea42b1b0eeac0fd7d107db75288a).

Friend, it's Congressman Jason Crow. I’m supporting Jessie Danielson to be our next Secretary of State. I know Jessie will defend our democracy, stand up to Donald Trump, and protect our right to vote. Her track record proves that she’s up for the job. Jessie built and led the coalition that passed the **Voter Access and Modernized Elections Act** , turning Colorado’s voting system into a national model for security and accessibility. She passed the **Automatic Voter Registration** and **Voting Rights for Voters With Disabilities** , expanding access to the ballot and making it easier for eligible Coloradans to participate in elections. As a former Army Ranger and now Member of Congress, I took an oath to defend the Constitution. I think about that oath every day. Colorado deserves a Secretary of State who shares this common belief and will fight every day to defend our country and protect our rights. Right on cue, my Republican opponent has already begun attacking
me.

Just one day after our primary win, he launched a website calling me
“extreme,” pushing baseless lies, and trying to smear my record of
standing up for Illinois families.

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20260511-split.BVNuuU&refcode=em20260511-61440&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1001&akid=61440%2E1407376%2EkC2zkV ]Image of Stratton's Republican opponent's website calling her
“extreme,” pushing baseless lies, and trying to smear her record of
standing up for Illinois families.

He saw what happened in our primary. He saw MAGA special interests pour
more than $10 million into attacking me. And now, he’s wasting no time
trying to pile on and tear down the movement we’re building together.

So, we need to fight
back — immediately.

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20260511-split.BVNuuU&refcode=em20260511-61440&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=61440%2E1407376%2EkC2zkV ]Please. Can you split $5 between Demand Justice PAC and
my campaign for U.S. Senate today? We have limited resources coming off
our primary win, and need your support to build back up and fend off these
attacks.

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20260511-split.BVNuuU&amount=5&refcode=em20260511-61440&t=1021&akid=61440%2E1407376%2EkC2zkV ]Donate $5 ››

The reality is, this attack website is just the beginning.

More money. More ads. More attacks — from my opponent, from special
interest groups, and from the same MAGA forces that tried to stop us
before. It’s all coming.

So right now we have a choice: we can let them define me in this race, or
we can fight back and keep Illinois moving forward — together.

I’m choosing to fight. And I’m asking you to stand with me.

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20260511-split.BVNuuU&refcode=em20260511-61440&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1022&akid=61440%2E1407376%2EkC2zkV ]If you’re able, please make a contribution today to help us push back

November. Whether it’s $5, $25, or whatever you can give, it truly makes a
difference right now.

— Juliana

| | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts.

By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina’s legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina.

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks.

She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina’s Income Tax—the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

Friend,
It’s been one year since I launched this campaign. Over the past year, I’ve traveled across Colorado’s 3rd District—meeting with farmers, workers, small business owners, and families in every corner of this district.
And I’ve heard the same thing again and again: Costs are too high. And people are getting squeezed.
I’ve talked to sweet corn farmers who are struggling to stay afloat. I’ve seen local economies taking a hit. I met a woman in Montezuma County who told me she’s paying five times more just to stay insured. And I’ve heard from families worried that our Western Slope way of life is at risk.
Meanwhile, Jeff Hurd supports over $900 billion in Medicaid cuts—putting 228,000 people in this district at risk of losing coverage and pushing rural hospitals closer to the brink.
In places like ours, healthcare isn’t optional. It’s essential.
I’m running because I’ll fight for the farmers, workers, and communities that make Colorado strong—and I’ll never stop working to bring costs down and put people first.
Together we can protect what matters—but we have to win. Will you chip in $15 or whatever you can today to help us keep building this campaign? [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/2605-q2-ak&amount=15]

It’s clear: Trump wouldn’t be doing this if he wasn’t TERRIFIED. He KNOWS Democrats are on track to end his MAGA trifecta in November.

# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)

Your **$5** donation will help my campaign have the resources to fight back against the $106 million war chest Greg Abbott is sitting on. He’s also backed by corporate donors who will spend whatever it takes to keep him in power so we need to be prepared. **This race is going to come down to turnout and persuasion, and that depends on a campaign powered by people like ours — not by billionaires, like Abbott’s.** If enough supporters step up at **$5** at a time, we can keep our momentum and win in November.

Gina

**" Heat stroke is suspected among 6 found dead in a shipping container at a rail yard near Texas border"** via AP**** - A South Texas medical examiner believes heat stroke may have led to the death of six people thought to be immigrants who were found Sunday afternoon inside a shipping container at a Union Pacific rail yard near the Mexico border in Laredo, Texas.

The people were found Sunday as workers were inspecting one of the containers, said Jose Baeza, a spokesperson for the Laredo Police Department.

Police and fire crews arrived at the scene shortly afterward. They confirmed that there were six people dead, five men and one woman, Baeza told reporters.

Dr. **Corinne Stern** , the Webb County Medical Examiner, is conducting autopsies and completed one for a 29-year-old Mexican woman who died of hyperthermia, or heat stroke. "I've ruled that an accidental death," she said. "I believe that the remaining individuals probably all succumbed to heat stroke as well, but their exams are not completed at this time, so I will not rule on their cause and manner yet."

Stern found identification cards and cellphones that indicate the deceased may be from Mexico and Honduras, but fingerprints were taken and shared with U.S. Border Patrol to help confirm their identities and nationalities through the Missing Alien Program.

The medical examiner's office also contacted the Mexican consulate after identifying the woman.

"This was a horrific scene," Stern added, also noting that immigrant deaths is a common occurrence in the ten-county region her office covers. "This spring has been busier than it was this time last year," the medical examiner said. (_[AP](https://substack.com/redirect/29cc1938-58b1-416f-9213-1ac5d5cff17d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" In parched Texas, a state fund to boost water projects falls almost $3 billion short of demand"** via [The Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/0a4efa6b-0db9-4099-9e3d-b1d9215fa837?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Colleen DeGuzman** - As Texas struggles to meet the needs of a rapidly growing population, a state fund had $1.28 billion available this year to support projects that could deliver water even in a severe drought.

Unfortunately, 23 worthy projects requested a total of $4.2 billion, prompting the state to deny 13 of them -- the first time the SWIFT fund had to say no to an applicant in its 11-year history.

It was lamentable timing for a state plagued by a brutal drought and aging water infrastructure.

"We have more demand than we actually have the capacity to fulfill this year," said **Marvin Cole-Chaney** , director of program administration and reporting for the Texas Water Development Board, which administers SWIFT, the State Water Implementation Fund for Texas. _([TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/0a4efa6b-0db9-4099-9e3d-b1d9215fa837?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Gas power leapfrogs wind for first time in 10 years in Texas' grid connection queue"** via [The Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/6a47132d-bed8-4dec-b62a-6149967cdaaa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Brandon Mulder** and **Chris Essig** - A decade ago, wind power was surging in popularity and attracting huge investments that made Texas a national leader in renewable energy. But today, gas generation is making a big comeback, driven by a wave of data centers flooding into the state.

For the last six months, the volume of gas generation in the Texas grid's interconnection queue -- the yearslong waiting list for electric generators wanting to connect to the grid -- has surpassed wind. It's the first time since January 2016 that gas has overtaken wind in the queue, a shift that reflects the policy and economic headwinds facing the wind industry and data centers favoring gas power as they seek to cash in on the artificial intelligence boom.

"The data center explosion and their desire for 24/7 power probably excited a lot of gas developers, and that gas queue got bigger," said University of Texas professor of energy regulation **David Spence**.

Like every power grid operator in the U.S., the Electric Reliability Council of Texas, or ERCOT, uses the interconnection queue to manage and plan for new power generation coming online. But not all projects in the queue ultimately reach completion. According to the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, or LBNL, only 22% of projects in ERCOT's queue actually get built, which is still the highest percentage of any grid in the nation. _([TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/6a47132d-bed8-4dec-b62a-6149967cdaaa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" New Texas A&M president confirmed as university seeks stability"** via AP**** - Regents on Wednesday unanimously appointed Susan Ballabina as president of Texas A&M, putting her in charge of the state's largest public university as it continues to deal with the fallout from its last president's resignation.

Ballabina, who assumes the role on May 11, most recently served as executive vice chancellor for the Texas A&M University System, overseeing day-to-day operations across its 12 universities and eight state agencies. Prior to that, she was former Texas A&M President Mark A. Welsh III's chief of staff.

Regents named Ballabina the sole finalist April 13. State law required them to wait 21 days before finalizing the hire. She initially served on the presidential search committee before recusing herself to apply for the job.

"I was a reluctant applicant. I wasn't sure that this was something I wanted to do, but after going through the process and preparing for the various interviews, I got more and more excited," Ballabina said during the regents' meeting after their vote.

The decision follows months of upheaval at the flagship campus after Welsh resigned amid political backlash over [a secretly recorded classroom discussion of gender identity](https://substack.com/redirect/942d6192-4603-4380-a92c-243d879cd045?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that was posted online.

The search unfolded as regents took a more assertive role in responding to controversy and shaping what can be taught, part of a broader political remaking of Texas colleges under new state laws. (_[AP](https://substack.com/redirect/7c97dd2a-742b-4e56-b396-d852e9209fd6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

Moritz** - **James Talarico** , a Texas Democratic primary candidate for U.S. Senate, frequently criticizes the influence of billionaires in politics and notably does not accept money from corporate political action committees.

However, this does not preclude PACs and billionaires from promoting his campaign. Lone Star Rising, a super PAC created to support Talarico, has raised approximately $9 million from politically active billionaires and millionaires, with nearly half sourced from a dark money group that does not disclose its donors.

Talarico has expressed support for banning super PACs and distances himself from Lone Star Rising, noting that federal law prohibits him from coordinating with the PAC or controlling its fundraising and spending.

"Legally, I cannot do anything about what any super PAC does, whether supporting me or not supporting me," Talarico told reporters. "We've got super PACs on all sides. We've got super PACs in the middle that are playing on both sides. It's nothing that we have control over." _([AAS](https://substack.com/redirect/e1dae46c-9329-4be7-8d47-ed1c1e7d38bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Texas reaches deal with youth camps over fiber‐optic rule tied to safety law"** via [CBS News](https://substack.com/redirect/1d874a31-096c-4d09-9c0c-612607d7a0e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Jack Fink** - The Texas Department of State Health Services has struck a deal with youth camps over a requirement that they install a fiber‐optic internet connection to operate this summer. A group of camps filed suit against the state last month after the mandate was included in a camp safety law approved by lawmakers last year. The agreement stays the court proceedings until March 1, 2027.

The legislation followed horrific flooding in Central Texas on July 4 that resulted in 25 campers and two counselors losing their lives at Camp Mystic. The camp's executive director also died.

Under the agreement, camps that maintain redundant internet service and comply with all other safety requirements will not have their licenses denied if they have not installed fiber‐optic service. The agency said alternative broadband options - including cellular, microwave, or satellite - are acceptable as long as they meet the definition of broadband under the Texas Government Code.

On Tuesday, Lt. Gov. **Dan Patrick** and House Speaker **Dustin Burrows** , R‐Lubbock, issued a joint statement aimed at giving camps more flexibility. They acknowledged that some camps were struggling to comply and that other forms of reliable redundant internet access exist. _([CBS News](https://substack.com/redirect/1d874a31-096c-4d09-9c0c-612607d7a0e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Texas prisons saw 2,500% increase in overdose deaths in 7 years, TDCJ leader says"** via [KERA News](https://substack.com/redirect/c91f5a5a-d860-4c80-9fff-48b41db4a8a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Toluwani Osibamowo** - Overdose deaths in Texas prisons jumped 2,480% over the past seven years, a state prison official told lawmakers this week as they consider ways to curb contraband in Texas correctional facilities.

There were 129 recorded overdose deaths among people in Texas Department of Criminal Justice custody last year, said **Bobby Lumpkin** , TDCJ's executive director. That's up from five such deaths in 2018.

The data was presented to senators Monday but has not been made publicly available online. It represents a relatively small portion of the 142,000 people Lumpkin said are currently in TDCJ custody.

"The root cause is a dependency and an addiction to that type of illicit substances," he told lawmakers during a Senate Committee on Criminal Justice hearing. "It unfortunately is an extension of the criminal element that even though they've been through the judicial system, been sentenced, they still depend back on that type of activity." _([KERA News](https://substack.com/redirect/c91f5a5a-d860-4c80-9fff-48b41db4a8a7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" TEA selects Connally schools superintendent to lead takeover"** via [The Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/0bcb3bb0-6985-4f45-b3fe-093f31c45dd5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Sneha Dey** - In a takeover of Connally ISD, the state brought in an educator from a neighboring Waco district to accelerate academic gains.

Texas Education Agency Commissioner **Mike Morath** picked **Josie Gutierrez** to lead the 2,000-student district, citing her success in improving outcomes and strengthening teacher retention as deputy superintendent and an assistant superintendent of human resources for Waco ISD.

Gutierrez is the latest superintendent Morath has appointed in recent weeks to helm districts after the commissioner took control from locally elected school trustees over poor academic performance.

Other state interventions include those in Fort Worth, Lake Worth and Beaumont. _([TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/0bcb3bb0-6985-4f45-b3fe-093f31c45dd5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" AG Ken Paxton leaves Odessa hanging after tax investigation"** via [The Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/dd680abd-1074-452e-8b50-0f32f3a36e3e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Carlos Nogueras Ramos** - Last October was like any other for most Odessa city employees. Parks employees unveiled a new sign. The police department gave a tour to homeschooled kids. A council member attended a fundraising event for culinary students.

But amid everyday responsibilities, top local officials were scrambling to respond to Texas Attorney General **Ken Paxton** 's demand that they justify a recently approved tax rate hike. The state had just passed a law that prohibited cities from raising taxes without completing financial audits. Paxton had singled out four cities, and Odessa was among them.

"To uphold my duty as the Attorney General to ensure that municipalities are following audit laws, I am formally launching an investigation into the City of Odessa to determine whether the new tax rate is illegal," Paxton wrote. "Furthermore, I am demanding that the new tax rate not be implemented until I complete my investigation."

City officials moved quickly, gathering hundreds of pages of documents, including minutes from relevant City Council meetings and evidence that the tax rate was published in a newspaper. By December 2025, Odessa had handed over the documents Paxton requested. _([TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/dd680abd-1074-452e-8b50-0f32f3a36e3e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**LOCAL GOVERNMENT**
**" Former Mayor Mike Rawlings launches campaign to relocate Dallas City Hall, revive downtown"** via [Dallas News](https://substack.com/redirect/35c6d004-9a53-4ae4-9126-1ebcc31cec3c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Devyani Chhetri** - **Mike Rawlings** is ramping up the fight over City Hall as questions grow over how to reshape downtown Dallas. Rawlings launched a coordinated campaign Thursday to build support for relocating City Hall, using newspaper and social media ads, a website and other outreach to promote redevelopment there, possibly for a sports arena and entertainment district.

In an interview with The Dallas Morning News, Rawlings said his efforts are designed to shift the City Council beyond wrangling over repair estimates and focus instead on how best to use the site as a catalyst to attract new business and reinvigorate its southern edge. "My fear about downtown is we're thinking too small," he said. "We've got to have a force to change this."

The campaign marks an escalation in the increasingly high-stakes fight over City Hall's future. It's been a clash of competing visions, centered on whether the council should invest in costly updates to the building or move government operations and pursue a different use for that large swath of land as the Dallas Mavericks look for a new home.

The council is expected to make that consequential choice in June after city staffers present a cost comparison of staying or leaving. Previous votes have indicated the mayor and eight council members support exploring relocation, while six members are opposed. _([DMN](https://substack.com/redirect/35c6d004-9a53-4ae4-9126-1ebcc31cec3c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Mayor John Whitmire's new city budget shrinks Houston's future deficits"** via [Houston Chronicle](https://substack.com/redirect/a07c62ec-45b8-4f49-a0b1-2e9d7e76d293?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s**Abby Church** - Finance projections at Houston City Hall show steps city officials took to close a budget deficit in the proposal Mayor John Whitmire announced Tuesday would significantly reduce future red ink.

Whitmire's proposed $7.5 billion budget includes a new $5 monthly fee on city trash customers to help the city's troubled Solid Waste Management Department, which has long struggled to pick up trash, recycling and yard waste on time. That fee would generate $24 million in new revenue -- a rare step at City Hall.

But the proposal would also change the structure of the city budget by moving the $117 million solid waste budget out of the strained general fund and into Houston Public Works, within the city utility system.

The mayor also proposes charging the utility system $104 million - or 5% of its annual gross revenues - for its pipes using the city right of way, money that also would flow into the general fund. _([HOU CHRON](https://substack.com/redirect/a07c62ec-45b8-4f49-a0b1-2e9d7e76d293?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Corpus Christi City Council votes to start talks on building a new desalination plant"** via [Spectrum News](https://substack.com/redirect/e7fc4294-751e-4fd7-bb9e-e8ef9000ea6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) -- As Corpus Christi's water crisis looms and city leaders scramble for solutions, the City Council has voted 6-2 to move forward with talks for a new company to build a desalination plant.

Houston-based AXE H2O is a two-month old company that says it can build a plant that can produce 150 million gallons of drinking water per day using natural gas, according to a report from The Texas Tribune. The city would pay $6.50 for 1,000 gallons of water.

According to **John Olson** , the company's chairman, the project would be a private venture and construction would take about two years. The company estimates it would cost about $1.3 billion to build.

Council members **Roland Barrera** and **Cynthia Campos** -- who made up the two votes against the project -- were skeptical, with Campos saying it sounded "too good to be true." _([Spectrum News](https://substack.com/redirect/e7fc4294-751e-4fd7-bb9e-e8ef9000ea6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" FBI says 6th Street shooter acted alone in March 1 mass shooting"** via [KXAN Austin](https://substack.com/redirect/b730d70e-9a87-4ff2-a46b-4a10ef296821?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s Dalton Huey - The FBI said Thursday that its investigation into the March 1 mass shooting in downtown Austin found no evidence that the gunman was directed by a foreign terrorist organization. The press release notes that investigators learned that the perpetrator, **Ndiaga Diagne** , had expressed admiration for former Iranian Ayatollah**Ali Khamenei** and held grievances over American and Israeli attacks against Iran.

The FBI also stated that Diagne, a 53-year-old Senegal-born man and naturalized U.S. citizen as of 2013, had legally purchased a handgun in August 2017 and a rifle in October 2017. Diagne used both of those guns in his attack on West Sixth Street, in which he killed three people and injured 15 others. Responding Austin police officers confronted and killed him minutes after he opened fire.

The three killed in the shooting were **Savitha Shan** , **Ryder Harrington** and **Jorge Pederson**. In the initial aftermath of the attack, FBI officials said that there were "indicators" that it was an act of terrorism. The FBI said Thursday that its investigation determined Diagne acted alone and had not received outside funding, operational support or direction for the attack.

He also had not been the subject of any prior FBI investigation, according to the press release. Investigators also said Diagne's "violent behavior" escalated due to "specific personal triggers and grievances" connected to the Iran war. The FBI found Diagne admired Khamenei, who had been killed in the U.S. and Israeli attacks one day before the shooting. _([KXAN](https://substack.com/redirect/b730d70e-9a87-4ff2-a46b-4a10ef296821?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

Ward** - Channelview-area leaders celebrated Wednesday after the Environmental Protection Agency ordered Waste Management and International Paper Co. to begin hauling toxic mud from a dioxin-filled waste pit that lurked in the San Jacinto River for decades.

"It's a good day to be in Harris County," said **Tom Ramsey** , the county commissioner for the area surrounding the waste pits, as he called the San Jacinto River the "lifeblood" of the region.

The cost estimate for cleanup of the underwater waste, known as the northern impoundment of the San Jacinto waste pits, has now climbed to a quarter of a billion dollars.

The companies do not have a mandated excavation date yet, though they must respond to the federal government within 10 days of the April 28 order. According to federal Superfund law, they could owe three times the total cost of work if the EPA has to take over cleanup efforts. _([HOU CHRON](https://substack.com/redirect/ae9af29c-4902-494d-ba1f-d84e11ace6ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**BUSINESS NEWS**
**" BlackRock invests $30M in Texas electrician training amidst data center boom"** via [KXAN Austin](https://substack.com/redirect/5dbfa794-eb36-4cfe-97d9-1311fe008bbb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s**Adam Schwager** -- Custom homebuilder **Gene Lantrip** has a slight problem. He's got a backload of about 15 houses right now, partially due to a recent boom of data centers in the region. "Oracle came in", he recalled "The next thing you know, they put out a call for 500 electricians"; Among those electricians were ones who helped put the finishing touches on the homes Lantrip builds.

"Local guys right now in Abilene, starting out and make $15 an hour, the good ones make up for $25 an hour," Lantrip says. He says the data center companies are willing to pay double -- and he can't compete. "So our electricians, what they started doing was hiring inexperienced young kids and teaching them the trades -- on-the-job training," he said. "My electrician used to have a team of about 12 guys... Now they have one lead guy and about five young kids... When they had 12 guys, they can knock out three houses, but now it takes them all day to do one house."

This comes at a time where the demand for Lantrip's services are as high as ever. "There's like 14,000 temporary workers out there working in right now, and they all need a place to stay," he said.

BlackRock, one of the largest private equity firms in the world, faces similar problems. "As the largest investor in infrastructure, we hear in every project, 'We don't have enough workers. We can't find the workers. We're challenged. We're going to have delays," BlackRock CEO **Larry Fink** said. "When you have delays in your projects, that means it costs more money." _([KXAN](https://substack.com/redirect/5dbfa794-eb36-4cfe-97d9-1311fe008bbb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Nvidia could bring thousands of jobs to Austin. Here's how."** via [Austin American-Statesman](https://substack.com/redirect/097b5775-3708-49bc-81c0-b0034ae82b60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Karoline Leonard** - Nvidia CEO **Jensen Huang** speaks with a Disney robot during an Nvidia conference focusing on artificial intelligence in San Jose, Calif., on March 16. The artificial intelligence chipmaker announced a partnership with glassmaker Corning to build three new factories in North Carolina and Texas, creating more than 3,000 new jobs.

The world's most valuable company might bring thousands of jobs to Austin as Nvidia ups its investment in Texas.

Artificial intelligence chipmaker Nvidia Corp. and glassmaker Corning Inc. announced plans to build three new plants dedicated to manufacturing light and glass technologies for AI manufacturing in North Carolina and Texas.

The companies, which both have significant business ties to the Austin area, promised to create more than 3,000 jobs at the factories. _([AAS](https://substack.com/redirect/097b5775-3708-49bc-81c0-b0034ae82b60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Is Brownsville getting a refinery? America First CEO is confident; industry analyst skeptical"** via [MyRGV.com](https://substack.com/redirect/6b75f036-6d37-4d14-bcbc-50a9f1200494?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Steve Clark** - When **Donald Trump** announced on Truth Social March 10 that Brownsville would be the site of the first U.S. oil refinery to be built in 50 years, it seemed to come out of the blue.

But in fact, Port of Brownsville officials have been in communication with the principals behind the proposed America First Refining (AFR) project for about a dozen years, according to Brownsville Navigation District Chairman **Steve Guerra**.

Back in June 2024, AFR founder and CEO **John Calce** announced that his company (then Element Fuel Holdings) had completed the site preparation and pre-construction work for a large oil refinery at the port. In a statement, he said the company had secured the permits necessary to construct and operate a refinery with a capacity of more than 160,000 BPD, or "approximately 6.7 million gallons, per day of finished gasoline, diesel and jet fuel."

Reuters reported at the time that Calce had tried before to build a refinery at the port, through start-up firms ARX Energy and Jupiter Brownsville LLC, one such attempt resulting in a bankruptcy filing. _([MY RGV](https://substack.com/redirect/6b75f036-6d37-4d14-bcbc-50a9f1200494?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_
