Bangor handed hundreds of thousands in federal grant money to Food and Medicine, a nonprofit where Democratic gubernatorial candidate Troy Jackson worked, that campaigned against the voter ID referendum and in favor of a convicted killer for the City Council.
"The name sounded familiar since while running for City Council a couple years ago there were flyers mailed to residents of Bangor with this name on the flyer supporting specific individuals from a particular political party. In addition to these mailers, it appears that there were paid canvassers that listed "Food & Medicine" HQ address as the address of record," said former Bangor City Council Candidate Philip Henry in a [post](https://substack.com/redirect/64a13d87-035c-456c-8bd7-b4e023ab30c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) calling out the city's funding for the partisan organization.
According to Bangor's most recent [report ](https://substack.com/redirect/19de4ded-3a3f-44ca-983f-a895398c217f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)on its use of federal American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) grant funds, the City Council decided to award $336,342 of its $20.48 million in ARPA funding to the 501c(4) dark money nonprofit Food and Medicine.
The nonprofit does not have to disclose its individual donors and can theoretically accept an unlimited amount of funds and use those funds to endorse and work to elect candidates, serving as a potential workaround for donors who prefer not to have their campaign contributions made public.
Food and Medicine actively intervened in the most recent Bangor City Council election in November, campaigned against the failed voter ID referendum, and employed, or currently employs, former Maine Senate President and current Democratic gubernatorial candidate Troy Jackson.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..6noXqlo3xT8FKzQua1HrAliuL6pauP2x5hWO-FffBG4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=197231322)
The city earmarked $75,000 of the grant funds for Food and Medicine to build "raised bed gardens in underserved neighborhoods" as part of its "collective gardens," and the other $261,342 went to their workforce development program.
Strangely, Food and Medicine's Form 990 [tax filing](https://substack.com/redirect/20c1121c-d641-4e47-9ec8-0c909d8b59f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for 2024, shows that the organization drew in $661,854 but does not list any income under the "government grants" section of the tax documents, despite receiving money from the Bangor grant in that year.
Though the funding may be for innocuous purposes, it, of course, frees other resources for more political aims.
According to Food and Medicine's [website](https://substack.com/redirect/46c0599c-450e-40d1-a015-35b7d0ef290f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), they endorsed three left-wing candidates for the Bangor City Council: Daniel Carson, Susan Faloon, and Angela Walker.
Walker, notably, is a killer who was convicted after brutally killing a Canadian tourist on Old Orchard Beach by beating him and suffocating him by forcing sand down his throat.
Food and Medicine did more than just endorse the candidates; they actively [campaigned ](https://substack.com/redirect/1f350179-6e4b-4f12-8f98-47efb808105d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)on their behalf, sending out mailers and knocking on more than 3,000 doors for the candidates.
Henry told The Maine Wire that Food and Medicine's canvassers did all of Walker's door-knocking for her.
According to the [Bangor Daily News](https://substack.com/redirect/1f350179-6e4b-4f12-8f98-47efb808105d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Food and Medicine executive director Jack McKay has appeared as a speaker at a Graham Platner campaign event, though they have not officially endorsed the Senate candidate.
According to Maine State Ethics Commission [filings](https://substack.com/redirect/dc894fe7-3846-4824-9a36-1847f29b4cc5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Food and Medicine spent $9,759 campaigning against the voter ID referendum.
Outside their more overt political action, the organization also has close ties with Troy Jackson, who listed them as his employer on his last statement of income [filing ](https://substack.com/redirect/521b46b4-592d-4427-8ba1-3ddd30ae3577?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)during his time in the state Senate.
It appears that Jackson continued working with the dark-money organization after his time in the legislature was up, as he appeared on their [website ](https://substack.com/redirect/2629f82b-debe-4718-8e83-6c3f1d05df7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)as a project's organizer at least as recently as May 16, 2025, the day he first announced his gubernatorial campaign.
Based on archived versions of the site, he was removed from it sometime between May and July, though it is not clear whether he has actually stopped working for them.
The Maine Wire reached out by phone to Food and Medicine, but they did not answer.
The official press email address on Jackson's website is inactive, and the candidate did not answer his phone or respond to a voicemail asking about his association with the dark money group.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6ec0a925-b88a-4eb7-9304-6efbfef799dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Jackson's gubernatorial campaign [filings](https://substack.com/redirect/0fec9657-2bac-4733-94c0-2ca5f70ac7d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) reveal that Food and Medicine's director and deputy director have both made multiple direct contributions to his campaign, though the organization has not currently endorsed him.
Food and Medicine also [operates ](https://substack.com/redirect/835015cf-f8af-4be9-9b2a-2ca157e050d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)under the trading name Maine Jobs with Justice and has [ties ](https://substack.com/redirect/ad7f0ccb-479b-4fbe-9cb4-21009884e1da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)to the larger Washington D.C.-based Jobs with Justice 501(c)(4), which lists them as part of their "network."

Peter,

Three times now deranged lunatics have tried to assassinate President Trump.

Three times.

Each time they could have succeeded.

If the president in question was Joe Biden or Barack Obama, I’m confident there would be no objections to building a White House ballroom to ensure the safety of our president.

**After last Saturday 's attempted assassination at the White House Correspondents Dinner**, even one prominent Democrat senator advised his colleagues, liberal non-profit organizations, and others on the left to drop the Trump Derangement Syndrome and build the ballroom.

Peter, It's Becca. **I’ve been thinking a LOT about last week.** About the messages I read from teachers who told me they’re proud to have a fighter for their students and their public schools. About the moms and dads who said they’re relieved to know someone is still fighting to lower costs, protect their kids’ futures, and defend their freedoms. About the grandparents who told me they’re in this because they want the next generation to inherit a democracy that still belongs to the people. About the nurses, small business owners, union workers, caregivers, students, and neighbors who reached out to say: _**we’re glad you’re running again — and we’re with you.**_ I can’t tell you what that means to me. And I just want to start with this: _**Thank you.**_ Launching my campaign for re-election was about making one thing clear: this movement still belongs to the people. Not corporations. Not special interests. Not the backroom deal-makers who think they get to call the shots. People like **you** — showing up, speaking out, chipping in, and proving that real power comes from the ground up. **Those messages are what I’ll carry with me through this campaign and through every fight ahead. Because the work now is to turn that hope into organizing power, into conversations at doors and on phones, into the resources we need to reach every single voter in this country before the November elections.** [_**I know not everyone can give every time, and I don’t take it lightly when you do. But if you’re able today, will you click here and chip in $5, $10, or even $50 to help keep this people-powered campaign moving with real momentum?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131214783/620323261/-522538093?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZjgwZWYyYS04YjRkLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=S0Pv3vTi8YEA8ZgtVoYv_ubtxp7mvgMF5XUtgesWbjE=) Because here’s what last week made crystal clear: People are fed up with an economy that isn’t working for them. People are tired of watching basic rights get chipped away. And people want leaders who will actually fight and not back down when the going gets tough. **I can promise you this: I’m not interested in playing it safe. I’m in this fight because too many people can’t afford for us to lose it.** **[JUMP INTO THE FIGHT!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131214784/620323262/-522538093?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZjgwZWYyYS04YjRkLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=S0Pv3vTi8YEA8ZgtVoYv_ubtxp7mvgMF5XUtgesWbjE=)** You all know I’ve taken on tough fights before — for working families, for LGBTQ+ rights, for our democracy and I’m ready to keep doing it. But I can’t do it alone. This campaign is powered by people choosing to step up and say, “I’m in.” **[So if you didn’t get a chance last week — or if you did and you’re ready to go even further — click here today to help us build on this momentum!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131214785/620323263/-522538093?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZjgwZWYyYS04YjRkLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=S0Pv3vTi8YEA8ZgtVoYv_ubtxp7mvgMF5XUtgesWbjE=)** This is just the beginning. [Accept invitation to the 47th President Founders Club](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)

But yes, most people would dream of receiving an email like this one.
[](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
[Accept invitation here:](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
I personally created the **47th President Founders Club** for one reason only:
To permanently honor the patriots who founded and carried the entire MAGA movement from Day One! The ones who never wavered, never surrendered, and refused to let them destroy our country twice.

##### We're republishing this piece today from independent journalist [Jonathan Larsen](https://open.substack.com/users/23328754-jonathan-larsen?utm_source=mentions), whose reporting we follow closely and whose work consistently fact-checks the kind of administration spin most newsrooms now repeat without question. Larsen's latest takes apart President Trump's claim, made on Fox News after Saturday's shooting outside the White House Correspondents Association dinner, that the alleged shooter "hates Christians." Larsen pulled both the alleged manifesto and archived posts from Caltech's Christian Fellowship, where the suspect was reportedly a group leader organizing discussions on the Apostles' Creed and the forgiveness of sin. The piece is a short, sourced demolition of an easily-told lie--exactly the kind of small but load-bearing fact-check that corporate political reporters used to do reflexively, and now mostly don't.

Then read the piece below. He earns the support.
##### _**-- Editor's note, Blue Amp Media**_

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/54649b81-18d0-4763-a86d-98cca132562c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Cole Allen, subdued at the Washington Hilton Saturday after allegedly firing shots just outside the White House Correspondents Association dinner. (Uncredited / Pres. Donald Trump [photo](https://substack.com/redirect/5218081d-cff4-46c3-b205-c0763cf946be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).)
Pres. Donald Trump [said](https://substack.com/redirect/92a43389-adcf-48a4-83a7-b57e0b4ddf15?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Fox about the accused shooter at Saturday's White House Correspondents Association dinner that, "When you read his manifesto, he hates Christians."
In fact, the alleged gunman's "manifesto" reflects a Christian grappling with what his faith calls on him to do and not do.
And postings I found from his college Christian group show that Cole Allen wasn't merely a member, he was a leader.
In the message that Allen [reportedly](https://substack.com/redirect/5eaa6e3e-2ccb-49fd-ae7f-79d2fb091185?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) sent shortly before the shooting, he writes, "Turning the other cheek when *someone else* is oppressed is not Christian behavior; it is complicity in the oppressor's crimes."
Allen's view appears to have been that resorting to violence to stop violence was Christian behavior. It's almost a variation on the "just war" theory that Pope Leo XIV and Vice President JD Vance recently debated regarding Iran.
Allen's alleged message appeared to refer to the Iranian girls school demolished by a U.S. missile, killing 180 people, most of them children. He also cited other violence carried out by the U.S. government and, allegedly, individuals in it:
> "Turning the other cheek is for when you yourself are oppressed. I'm not the person raped in a detention camp. I'm not the fisherman executed without trial. I'm not a schoolkid blown up or a child starved or a teenage girl abused by the many criminals in this administration."
Ten years ago, Allen was a student at the California Institute of Technology, and a member of the Caltech Christian Fellowship (CCF). But not just a member.
In June 2015, he was [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/f034aaf7-4f7a-4761-a688-eb47f8ad8fb9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as a new large-group coordinator. The blog posting read, "Pray that Cole will be able to manage his time well, especially since he is taking ME 72 next year."
In October that year, Allen and another coordinator led a discussion on "God the Father." It was, the [notice](https://substack.com/redirect/07ac917b-32a4-4bf4-ba7e-e14a5b18f38b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) said, part of a series about the Apostles' Creed, the fourth-century affirmation of basic Christian beliefs, including the trinity, the resurrection, and the forgiveness of sin.
The following month, Allen [brought his pastor](https://substack.com/redirect/07abb3fa-e73f-41c8-8386-5537027e5d55?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to meet with CCF members. The subject was "the forgiveness of sin."
Another post indicates that Allen was still a large-group coordinator almost a year later, in September 2016.
Despite Allen's alleged attempt at a moral defense of his actions, the message he's said to have sent falls short morally and in Christian terms.
"I am no longer willing to permit a pedophile, rapist, and traitor to coat my hands with his crimes," the message says. But after listing the dinner staff and guests as not at all targets, it also says they're acceptable collateral damage.
> "I would still go through most everyone here to get to the targets if it were absolutely necessary (on the basis that most people *chose* to attend a speech by a pedophile, rapist, and traitor, and are thus complicit) but I really hope it doesn't come to that."
That's a justification that neither Christianity nor any moral code accept for murder. It's possible, however, that Allen, if he's guilty, understood and accepted that.
The message he allegedly sent Saturday night says, "I don't expect forgiveness."

Allen's alleged message appeared to refer to the Iranian girls school demolished by a U.S. missile, killing 180 people, most of them children. He also cited other violence carried out by the U.S. government and, allegedly, individuals in it: "Turning the other cheek is for when you yourself are oppressed. I'm not the person raped in a detention camp. I'm not the fisherman executed without trial. I'm not a schoolkid blown up or a child starved or a teenage girl abused by the many criminals in this administration." Ten years ago, Allen was a student at the California Institute of Technology, and a member of the Caltech Christian Fellowship (CCF). But not just a member. In June 2015, he was as a new large-group coordinator. The blog posting read, "Pray that Cole will be able to manage his time well, especially since he is taking ME 72 next year." In October that year, Allen and another coordinator led a discussion on "God the Father." It was, the said, part of a series about the Apostles' Creed, the fourth-century affirmation of basic Christian beliefs, including the trinity, the resurrection, and the forgiveness of sin. The following month, Allen to meet with CCF members. The subject was "the forgiveness of sin." Another post indicates that Allen was still a large-group coordinator almost a year later, in September 2016. Despite Allen's alleged attempt at a moral defense of his actions, the message he's said to have sent falls short morally and in Christian terms. "I am no longer willing to permit a pedophile, rapist, and traitor to coat my hands with his crimes," the message says. But after listing the dinner staff and guests as not at all targets, it also says they're acceptable collateral damage. "I would still go through most everyone here to get to the targets if it were absolutely necessary (on the basis that most people chose to attend a speech by a pedophile, rapist, and traitor, and are thus complicit) but I really hope it doesn't come to that." That's a justification that neither Christianity nor any moral code accept for murder. It's possible, however, that Allen, if he's guilty, understood and accepted that. The message he allegedly sent Saturday night says, "I don't expect forgiveness." Peter,

Here’s the truth: Republicans are focused on one thing—bringing your health care costs DOWN.

We’re pushing real price transparency so you know costs upfront. We’re fighting to increase competition to lower prescription drug prices. And we’re cutting the red tape that’s driving up costs—especially for families and rural communities here in North Carolina.

That’s the kind of common-sense approach people have been asking for.

If Democrats take the House, they’ll have the power to reverse course—more mandates, more bureaucracy, and more control from Washington. And history shows what that means: higher costs, fewer choices, and more pressure on already-stretched family budgets.

We’ve seen this movie before.

So I want you to think about what that would mean for your household, Peter. If Democrats take the House, do you think things will get BETTER or WORSE for healthcare affordability? name: AOC
subject: "Controversial"
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
When you fight really entrenched power, that power will fight you back.
#
"Why are you considered controversial?", someone recently asked me. I think there are a couple of reasons.
When you fight really entrenched power, **that power will fight you back**.
They cannot be seen attacking the message, because that makes them look bad — so they attack the messenger. There will never be an uncontroversial messenger for challenging the structures of power keeping wages low.
Secondly, I think my presence as someone who was a waitress... I’m not supposed to be there, according to them, and I’m not bought. There’s a real class aspect to this.
**There are a lot of people who think if you don’t make a lot of money, it’s reflective of your intelligence and your capacity as a human being**. There's a very real, built-in denigration and devaluing of people because of the class that they are in.
And of course, I’m a woman and I’m Latina. My mere existence is subversive in the place that I am.
I also don’t act in a way that women are supposed to act in a society like this. You’re coming at me crazy, I’m not going to be deferential to you.
That makes a lot of classist, ageist, misogynist, and racist people mad.
But together, we’ve built a movement fighting _against_ entrenched power and _for_ transformative change — from Medicare for All to democratizing fundraising power in politics.
[Help us continue the fight with a grassroots contribution today.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260511-2.jdBIKZ&refcode=em20260511-11392-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=11392%2E2526796%2EmAM8Ku)

In solidarity,
Alexandria

Derek, Our mid-month deadline is quickly approaching, and meeting our fundraising goal is key to our mission of winning back the House and Senate. So, today we’re asking you to chip in $7. $7 because we have one chance to take back Congress and slam the brakes on Trump’s agenda. $7 because this is a grassroots movement, which means we rely on supporters like YOU to help fund our work. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131216061/620327584/-201694504?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNjU4MDkxNi05MDRkLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=qnUsahZfi-qRtb9K22Zocvu2lA2ruafeQIRSaw-kk44=&emci=02dfaaf6-874d-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=d6580916-904d-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=9494239)

| | Coming off of Mother's Day weekend, I am thinking about how we can better support working families during this affordability crisis. Right now, working families are being pushed to the brink by the rising cost of child care. **In communities across Northwest Washington and around the country, parents are struggling to afford safe, reliable care while balancing jobs, bills, and everyday expenses. In many cases, child care costs now rival rent or mortgage payments — forcing families to make impossible choices about work, savings, and their future.** At the same time, child care providers and early learning centers are facing staffing shortages, rising costs, and a lack of long-term support. We must act. [**That is why I am calling on my colleagues in Congress to help lower child care costs for working families by:**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131216062/620327585/1674767621?contactdata=CT9llEQhZZehGSGOf++TIvnt5ajLOgXvaORs/nwiKxNB6E7eyR5bxFlqJCUjFpgGf0bn/hAWRt+yFsgj+hI+b4XLOiuMwzx5LjFXtAef6dKg73ZG+GLDF0JmGaiAQqWgBqpopn+1o5JFMK3WjAj3UA==&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNjU4MDkxNi05MDRkLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=qnUsahZfi-qRtb9K22Zocvu2lA2ruafeQIRSaw-kk44=&emci=02dfaaf6-874d-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=d6580916-904d-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=9494239)

name: Sheriff Joe Arpaio
subject: Help Free Two Innocent Officers Before It's Too Late
body:
Patriot,
This is a disgrace...and every American who believes in law and order should be furious.
Two police officers—Josh Taylor and Brandon Dingman—are currently serving prison sentences for doing exactly what they were trained and ordered to do: respond to a dangerous call, use non-lethal force, and protecting their community.
Let me tell you what really happened, because the media and the District Attorney certainly won't.
On the night of July 4th, 2019, Officer Josh Taylor responded to a domestic disturbance call in Wilson, Oklahoma. When he arrived, he encountered Jared Lakey: a large, fully grown man walking naked down the street wearing nothing but socks.
Josh immediately recognized this situation for what it was: dangerous and unpredictable. Whether it was drugs, mental illness, or something else—this wasn't a man in his right mind. And Josh knew he couldn't handle it alone. He called for backup.
[Donate to Their Defense](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=44d671e7af3b482babc2c637007fae43&_e=XW2DstJ26_bPGl8DRAJp04zR1BsHqde3DawqdUa6P7Kmxht7I4mRl_rUZJaTEFF9tALT0gQ4XFW1w3YT4M9214ELzwytKIjT5DLkX34TOGhSKu4DvPjxD5F9Ucr7m_jwt9E1Jx0kfCtpMdC-oOTXG-zb8UosbWv6LC1JPGrTbfbn5ybYWLav04Y4d0X0-q6FoGnuzwW7fGpyF_e5oGWxE_BuIwhAo87ZUiyHE7GgTfZ5x3Re9vtesgGHbn-WOm2lQu8gwVWJ7o6wZo2LPOFk-QgXhJCDGBnZ8iPa6dtRBeYDR4FOwYU_juOKpEhNiGjH1dCn5FhjqZmiivt6kXJRHJz7ewy2clCZPIpESxqgEiwttK4sVxfTRbBkkaxpAp3DVawEoBTRyX1xbJDtt7_-77XuWGr7rH8BsPY1AmexbeTcS4s9QgowIONDeohcFijN)
Officer Josh Taylor
Officer Brandon Dingman
Officer Brandon Dingman arrived on scene, and the two officers tried to do what they were trained to do: safely and professionally bring Mr. Lakey into custody.
But Lakey was 350 pounds, combative, and resisting arrest. When verbal commands didn't work and physical restraint proved impossible, they turned to their department-issued, non-lethal tasers.
They deployed them multiple times, but Lakey kept tearing the barbs out. He was clearly not being fully affected by the tasers—and even after repeated attempts, the officers were unable to subdue him.
Eventually, Josh and Brandon were able to get his arms and cuffed him. They immediately called for medical assistance. An ambulance arrived. Lakey was taken to the hospital.
At that point, the officers had done everything they could—and everything right.
But tragically, Jared Lakey passed away two days later. The autopsy was inconclusive. He had an enlarged heart and lung issues. Drug screenings were unreliable due to the fluids pumped into his system at the hospital. There was no determined cause of death.
Even so, the department launched an internal review. Then the City Council reviewed the case too.
Both cleared the officers. That's two separate investigations concluding Josh and Brandon followed procedure.
Case closed, right?
Wrong.
A full year later, a politically motivated District Attorney, smelling an opportunity, dragged the case back up and charged these officers with second-degree murder.
Let that sink in: second-degree murder. He ignored the internal findings. He ignored the medical uncertainty. He ignored the fact that these officers never even laid a hand on Lakey's neck or airway.
They followed their training, used the gear they were issued, and even called for medical help.
But none of that mattered to a DA looking to make headlines.
Now, these two good cops, family men, community protectors, are sitting behind bars.
The National Center for Police Defense is fighting to overturn this injustice. We're supporting their legal appeals, helping their families, and backing efforts to remove the biased District Attorney who never should have touched this case in the first place.
But appeals are costly. And the longer this drags on, the longer Josh and Brandon sit in prison...separated from their families, their children, their lives.
That's why I'm writing you today. We need your help.
[Yes — I'll Donate Today](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=44d671e7af3b482babc2c637007fae43&_e=XW2DstJ26_bPGl8DRAJp04zR1BsHqde3DawqdUa6P7Kmxht7I4mRl_rUZJaTEFF9tALT0gQ4XFW1w3YT4M9214ELzwytKIjT5DLkX34TOGiBkdQD73-j55ruvuWY4Wghn1EfHgzNmCltzEMKCLYUOvjAEorQfgfESxAvhwF8J93YM431FzN72GHqYP5IGS2XjX2c_884tmNlpa5x93wbH-QwMxwO2FTw58ZeLHJUU3LpzpaaQEx3WDYGR2haHipHV9Fl4qufkHFVy5T7wnbssPxwEO_9244oa5FpaBhENJmJoM1NfdGgpfPMOSaDuN2CCnt2DLc4QkCSfwd6bUdp4pY7eWuPvzw37HqCJwJq2dHwYczOliMBVKrc0t9uIy6hOdpEyM-vx4cTFhrZSVvWChW1RmcrEAM9xSV7Zb5gDYPJpgtXcqfMYWdLkIANjhIL)
We need to raise funds to fuel the legal defense and appeal process. These officers deserve their freedom. They deserve a fair hearing. And they deserve to come home.
We cannot let this go unanswered. If we don't stand up now, more and more police officers will suffer the same fate: thrown to the wolves by political activists in prosecutor's clothing.
Josh and Brandon were railroaded, plain and simple. And now we need to right this wrong.
Will you step up today and donate to support their appeals?
## Stand With Josh & Brandon
Every dollar goes directly to their legal defense and appeals. Help bring them home.
[Click Here to Donate](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=44d671e7af3b482babc2c637007fae43&_e=XW2DstJ26_bPGl8DRAJp04zR1BsHqde3DawqdUa6P7Kmxht7I4mRl_rUZJaTEFF9tALT0gQ4XFW1w3YT4M9214ELzwytKIjT5DLkX34TOGjrKwlKli4H074-1VX1dqRsm9c_RV6r-b3BQ7Y-adXNOGGz0_g8qE_p_fi1Fzpxjyb7bqfmonb2k-THkjFm0prN8cmNYFXM7kK_e6PURaDLbHbHr88TftNDGa0r6XK9oABTfpk2G017_1uX03WNqFK0CCiRtqVnpJu-dm-MOeYeEpIttRKw4J-MU5yu-lTfPO2Su3SiSJYHpLNJJd77JkSKOtaoJnAFZXLPQVRT5JLwVGBzZ1lgTx4COyr2hKNYtgu29FCy-L2HHHnEm5zFgFS-S8WkrhC5iXZZ70wmuusbzhbktKxE-2VkIZrMJz_4QnHMAGZEzr1FS47WhktBXR3b)
Your generous gift goes to defending these officers and restoring justice. No family should have to go through this. No officer should be imprisoned for doing his job.
Let's send a message: we still back the badge—and we won't let politics destroy the lives of our heroes.
For justice,
Sheriff Joe Arpaio (ret.)
National Center for Police Defense | Defenders for Justice

But Lakey was 350 pounds, combative, and resisting arrest. When verbal commands didn't work and physical restraint proved impossible, they turned to their department-issued, non-lethal tasers. They deployed them multiple times, but Lakey kept tearing the barbs out. He was clearly not being fully affected by the tasers—and even after repeated attempts, the officers were unable to subdue him. Eventually, Josh and Brandon were able to get his arms and cuffed him. They immediately called for medical assistance. An ambulance arrived. Lakey was taken to the hospital. At that point, the officers had done everything they could—and everything right. But tragically, Jared Lakey passed away two days later. The autopsy was inconclusive. He had an enlarged heart and lung issues. Drug screenings were unreliable due to the fluids pumped into his system at the hospital. There was no determined cause of death. Even so, the department launched an internal review. Then the City Council reviewed the case too. Both cleared the officers. That's two separate investigations concluding Josh and Brandon followed procedure. Case closed, right? Wrong. A full year later, a politically motivated District Attorney, smelling an opportunity, dragged the case back up and charged these officers with second-degree murder. Let that sink in: second-degree murder. He ignored the internal findings. He ignored the medical uncertainty. He ignored the fact that these officers never even laid a hand on Lakey's neck or airway. They followed their training, used the gear they were issued, and even called for medical help. But none of that mattered to a DA looking to make headlines. Now, these two good cops, family men, community protectors, are sitting behind bars. The National Center for Police Defense is fighting to overturn this injustice. We're supporting their legal appeals, helping their families, and backing efforts to remove the biased District Attorney who never should have touched this case in the first place. But appeals are costly. And the longer this drags on, the longer Josh and Brandon sit in prison...separated from their families, their children, their lives. That's why I'm writing you today. We need your help. We need to raise funds to fuel the legal defense and appeal process. These officers deserve their freedom. They deserve a fair hearing. And they deserve to come home. We cannot let this go unanswered. If we don't stand up now, more and more police officers will suffer the same fate: thrown to the wolves by political activists in prosecutor's clothing. Josh and Brandon were railroaded, plain and simple. And now we need to right this wrong. Will you step up today and donate to support their appeals? Stand With Josh & Brandon Every dollar goes directly to their legal defense and appeals. Help bring them home. Your generous gift goes to defending these officers and restoring justice. No family should have to go through this. No officer should be imprisoned for doing his job. Let's send a message: we still back the badge—and we won't let politics destroy the lives of our heroes. For justice, Sheriff Joe Arpaio (ret.) National Center for Police Defense | Defenders for Justice

Iran Ceasefire on Life Support

Donald Trump declared Monday that the U.S.-Iran ceasefire is on ["massive life support"](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLGO6yAQRb8Gd45gjI1TULzGXV67pTWGIR4tBgvIZvfvV8knbH2le3TOx229IUdO9_94kC0trD77tZXHcYaYsdU71obfe47s8WdbQcLUy7FXak1xVZ233nlUriOrjJlHDfI6dbvdjIJhRCDpt-CGzWikQRNpI6W-6rlj-7qSo1IwwKyGC45qcHKaA0o9bU4JLTFSaZdC52OL7DA1rJ8hF0cXl48u2r21s4rhn4BFwNJ22jnG1yZg2fNBiZ5VwIL-4MS1FWyck4BlnA1MUvdvzZ4Lpt4RVgpcqI8cqK-P88ylCVi6Yv355Bi5TkZoeT-Q34yu_SHXl4XfAAAA__-vr3rY) -- giving talks a "1% chance" -- after rejecting Tehran's latest counteroffer as "totally unacceptable" and "a piece of garbage." Iran's foreign ministry called its proposal "reasonable and generous." The two sides remain stuck on the same core disputes: Washington demands Iran open the Strait of Hormuz before nuclear talks begin, while Tehran refuses to surrender that leverage. [Trump rejected](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckDtu6zAURFdDdTL4kSipYPEadX5tSuGKH_siFEmQ13ay-0DODlIPMDPnfFy3K2DEdPsPhzeVwuay26g-jhJiBmo3aARf9xzRwfe-SS51z8deiC3FTXTOOOtA2M4bMU3zOEi-6O5ulObauz0IBQrmJQQ-eb3Mel6mXVoVOjRnFR-FkErOQl1gFMpyPQfgg96tYAOH6Ctdqi-PPaKFRNA-Q67WX2w-umjuRKUx9Y_JlckVSvKvdkZMrhGfnsn1DdKDOzBhowqEOfWP4oB8-8XozxtdNa68MEZsemIDvx2A8T1Cf3DyNPInAAD__x7JcLY) the sequencing outright, calling Iran's demand to lift the blockade first a non-starter. Oil prices climbed on Monday on news of the breakdown, extending gains that have pushed energy costs sharply higher since the conflict began. [Iran vowed to fight on](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLFuwyAURb8Gb1iAgTgDQxdv6drRen48J6jYIMBx-_dV8gmdr3R1zvm6zTcIMez3T9jIlbbOPvm5lWPLa0zQ6h1qg59HisHD7zIroSwXhks573GWnXcePUjsyMnLZTRaiavtHs6SHLQ2eF2vZM0iLXlr0Ggr_OhRmi6415UwUqpBjXLowcgBhR1XENouKJkWEKm0vlA-lhgQ9gb1e00Fqce0ddE9WsuVDR9MTUxN53n2uNSdzvramZpieBI_sodGlakpFNj5CYW_9XgKkecSkCrPBEg8l5RThciPHRApN1giMTV1xfl8hhhDtRemxX2DEN8I7R_Fnk79BQAA__-yfH04) as no new negotiating sessions were scheduled, leaving the diplomatic path to ending the war narrower than ever. ★★★
SCOTUS Rewrites Redistricting Rules

The Supreme Court ruled that under the Voting Rights Act, [congressional districts can no longer be drawn along racial lines](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL1u5SAUhJ8Gd1hw_LsFxTbu7rZbWgc42CgYLMBx7ttHziOkG2mkGX3f_9f6Qh983P7hQSpXt9pk15qv43QhYS0blopfewre4luvIGDkYuBSrjGssrHKGovSNKTkNM1DD-LP2OxqluS01Loz_QQI0zANg3VWSDM66qBvvHqmxCAldDDLrsVBdkaMs0PRj9pI1gsMlGub6bx08AZjxfLhUjbUmnQ0Qe21noV1fxksDJb7vlujS6S7PD2D5YkMlmJSvQrP18PJr7JTLtxHjjzSzSkjT45vlPP7wGgp-7gxWJqs7Hn7EHwZJ9aL7UAffo7rLzx9KvgOAAD__wRleYg) -- but can be freely shaped by party affiliation. Observers are calling it a "new era of gerrymandering," with Southern Republican legislatures moving immediately to redraw congressional maps. Louisiana, Alabama, and Tennessee announced plans to redraw districts within days of the ruling. Republican strategist Karl Rove warned the rush could backfire, arguing that aggressive remapping [risks energizing Democrats](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0L2O4yAUQOGnwZ0juDZgFxTbuMu2W1rX_NhXwWABSXbefpR5hKmP9BXn3329I0VK-188vSktrC67tZXneYWYsdUda8P_R47k8GtbgYPqueyFWFNcReeMsw6F7bwRWk9yBD6r7jAKpZw2LbbROguDnmYVgtNyBq4Qhrkj86G4FAIGmMRwQykGy9UUkI9qs4KNHKMv7Vb89dwiWUwN6yPkYv3N5rOL5mjtqmz4w2BhsLTDHxTjpzFYjnz65N-VwWLxvJD2xGCRkwY56b7kl-_fWFLti3dUWyHbKO39hvYRqHgGS1eMu94UI1Wl2cj3E-lH79ovRr0MfAcAAP__WtJ4Hg) heading into the 2026 midterms -- a warning that has landed with a thud in state capitals. The ruling gives the GOP a structural advantage on paper, but the window to implement new maps before midterms is tight. Several Republican strategists are urging restraint, warning that overreach could produce a backlash that [undoes whatever seat gains](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD2O5CAQhU-DM7eKwr8BwSZkvemGVhmwu7QYLKCnZ-b0I_cRJnrBk97P9---3IkDx_0vHV7nui0uuaXm53FuIVEtO5VKn48U2NHXuiDg0ELfSrnEsMjGaWcdSdt4Lcdx6juEeWge2mFHk5pxGsHNfbfN4FXf-XlYJ0-g5ob1FQW9lKhwkupGvVQWhmkj6IbVStEBBZ_rLfvzuQa2FCuV_1vK1t9sOpqgH7WeRag_Ao1Ac6bAlW26TIEm-lcRaA7a6ZujF2iuQoEGeoFGSoHmfbPd09lm77jUzLZy3NsX5XgpwCzVMI5N1u58cQhchlF0sB_E4b2h_gLZh8afAAAA___YwHkW) new maps might otherwise deliver. ★★★
Trump Eyes Gas Tax Freeze

President Trump confirmed Monday he's suspending the federal gas tax, [telling CBS News](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL2ynSAUhZ8GO5zNVlALijR0N21KZwuoTFAc4MR73j7jeYTbrWLN-vn-fM1fFGI4t990eJ3rOrvk5ppfx7XGRLVsVCp97ykGR-9lRkDFQXIh5jPOonHaWUfCNl6LYRhljzCpZtfk5NoBWZIgp5G898squw4mZZW3wjZBP1EghcAOR9G1JEVnQY0rQa8WK1gPFH2ubfbXa4nB0lmp_F1Ttr616Wii3mu9Cut-MTQMzX3f7atQTY7ej4GhKTXlN0Nz-rswNFeKoQb7yKecoQHJ0AjB0Hwu89U7nynyjQqv9M2vHKwvfA_bzm_KPGQ6GZoJACepFMDA0DRZu-sOMYaiBtbDdlCIn4n1B0T_afwfAAD__3b7g_c): "We're going to take off the gas tax for a period of time." Gas has topped $6 a gallon -- more than 50% above pre-war levels -- as the Iran conflict extends into its 11th week. Congressional Republicans are joining the push, with Energy Secretary Chris Wright confirming Sunday the administration is ["open to all ideas"](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0LFutDAQBOCnMR1od8GGv3DxN3SXNiVabANWDEa2L1zePuIeIfVI32jm8zE92Ad_rB-8O53KMtlop5Ke-7mEyCWvnAu_thi85Z95IiBVg6wRpyNMWFltjWU0ldPY94PsCP6patPDIJ0yqjfOzSgVKzA99JaHdumgm-fK65sCiUgtDdg2LLE1oIaFoVOzQdEBB5dKk9z5nIM3fBTOX0tMxjUm7lXQWylnFu1_QaOg8bquhl8-5jsVNN6-oBGkoBFB0PheVa-c68KvOj_z6Y7s41Ffya9bqZK25-VD8Fn1ooN1Zx_eTeUPx3xr-g0AAP__3pBx8Q) on fuel costs. The federal gas tax is 18.4 cents per gallon -- critics note that suspending it won't make a meaningful dent in a $6-plus fill-up. Democrats are hammering the spike while Republicans in battleground districts go quiet. Trump envisions the cut as temporary -- phasing back in once prices fall --, but [analysts say](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0LFyhCAYBOCnwQ6HH0WPgiKN3aVN6fz8oDJBcYCLl7fP3D1C6p35dna_7vMdQwzH-om7N7kus0turvmxn0tMWMuKpeJzSzE4_LWzFHLgQnGA-YgzNM44cgjUeAPjeFO9FHpoNuN0L4EsovUjaKE0Eo0DLlpbp0elmmBelFAAspM36FpU0JEYbguKfrAErBcYfa5t9ufDxkB4VCzfS8rkW0p7E81W61lY98HkxOR0XVdLh6VXyOT04pmchGJyAmByeo_ilI41-1L4mk6-YuEVnzxkPPiFud3qHpts3HmFGEMZRtaLdccQ3431Hwf9GPkXAAD__4BzdIw) even a zero gas tax wouldn't bring pump prices close to pre-war levels.

Alabama Attorney General Steve Marshall filed a [petition with the Supreme Court](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckMGupCAQRb9GdxhAUd-CxWzcvdnO0hRQ2JVXigFsu_9-0vMJs7vJTU5Ozp_v9RuI6dh-w44217iGFNaar_2MnKCWDUqF1yMxBXi7VUs9CmmEUuvBq2qDDT6A8i1aNU2zGbT8GtuHxWjMbIx3bgxK-ThMMqL50lG6wUklW7IflDRK6V7Pqu_AqN7LcY4gh9F51QwSGHPtMp6XY_JwVCg_MWWPnU97y_ZR61ma_lejl0Yv9313Mb0OvMvnb_RyJqZKvjR6AQYHOwjYxA4_WES5zow7Cp-uXMXJ8P5MDiIgsAjoqdATheN0i4yBSs3kKx2buCG32YbzJmYq49QMctuB-J9U_Y-GT6v_BgAA__93qITk) to overturn a prior ruling that forced the state to draw a majority-minority district that favored Democrats.

Republican candidates who played active roles in contesting the 2020 election are [on track to win](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0L2O4yAUBeCnwZ0t7jUmTkGxDV223dK6_NhGi8ECEs-8_Sh5hOmPzjn6_j2WB4UY0vaXDq9KWxeX3dLK8zjXmKnVjWqjrz3H4OjbLMhR9nzqAZYUF-icctYR2M4ruN3mSSC_y25XIKzhlgt_N9PoOQhHMI93kn6VqzSmC-pdxScAHHGGcaAJRsvlvBIX0lhgglP0pQ3Fn08Tg6XUqP5fc7F-sPnootpbOysb_zDUDPV1XcNFdQ9pazmdubZ3jKE-cwwt2MpQvzcZaj4x1AAMtY_etpBTv-WXLymX3vkUfKn9x4Ch7opy5xViDFXemODbQSF-DrRfeL0U_gQAAP__HbZ6pQ) governor primaries in Arizona, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin -- three states whose governors will oversee the 2028 presidential election.

Confirmation before Jerome Powell's term expires on May 15 is expected. Warsh inherits a central bank still fighting inflation -- and a president intent on shaping rate policy.

Republicans need the package to advance immigration enforcement -- but the ballroom funding is fracturing the caucus.

Louisiana, Alabama, and Tennessee are moving to [redraw their maps](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0LFyhCAUheGnwc4dQEAtKNLYbdqUzhVQ7gTBgbvZ5O0zm0dIfeZ8xf9xX--ACfPxDmewlfbVF79SfZzXngpQO6ARfMeS0MPPtkouTc91L8Sa0yo6b73zIFwXrBjHSSvJZ9NFq_w8j8Ztk9J8g1GZYeBq0-BNAMG3qUP7orgWQg5yEsMNtBgcN9MOXJnNCaY4pFDpVsP12BI6yATtcy_VhZsrZ5dsJLoaG96YXJhcKIaIKb02JpdYzpDDszG5ODgvwCMzuehp5HoWfQ0eG1V0hPnodzwi9a08KIaa-0ZA4XXsqvXXE1PCZkam-HEC_vkd_SPVl5W_AQAA__99d3kz) after the Supreme Court weakened the Voting Rights Act -- swapping racial district criteria for partisan ones. The redistricting rush before the November midterms could backfire by energizing Democratic voters.

Here are the candidates I'm voting for in June. I hope you will consider voting for them too!

# Rose’s Ballot
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/cGsJSQHOBFq?e=8c53948e4c&c2id=06d66eac9b545d55bb613c1fdc65532c)
| | Hello friends,
Politicians rarely tell us who they’re voting for or what they really believe in. So in the spirit of transparency, I want to share with you some of my favorite candidates running for office in California.
**I’m voting for Oliver Ma for CA Lieutenant Governor**. He is a civil rights lawyer who has fought back against slumlords, ICE, and apartheid. He’s serious about making California serve our people, not corporations and special interests.
**I’m voting for Jane Kim for CA Insurance Commissioner**. Her push for Disaster Insurance For All is an innovative, people-first approach to protecting families across California — especially in our District where fires and flooding are a constant risk.
**I’m voting for Tom Steyer for Governor**. Steyer supports non-profit single-payer healthcare, will tax billionaire and close corporate tax loopholes, and protect clear air laws and make polluters pay. When my family lived in Oakland 15 years ago, I was on the Steering Committee of the Local Clean Energy Alliance. We were aligned with Tom in our fights against PG&E and oil companies against ballot propositions that would have increased their stranglehold on our energy. On a personal level, Tom’s wife Kat Taylor is a friend and a member of a non-profit I co-founded, WetheChange, a collective of women CEO’s of B Corps and mission driven businesses working toward an inclusive and regenerative economy.
**If you haven’t already done so, I urge you to fill out your mail-in ballot early, or make a plan to vote in-person on June 2nd. And if you can, donate a few dollars so we can finish the primary election strong.**

May 11, 2026

Republican gubernatorial candidate Erin Stewart is on the ropes. According to the Hartford Courant, she used public funds to purchase items such as diapers, club memberships, birthday dinners etc. while she was the Mayor of New Britian. She issued a response stating:

"The timing of these attacks is no coincidence - the moment public polling showed Ned Lamont under 50%, the Democratic machine, their allies in New Britian City Hall, and our Republican opponents all went into hyperdrive. Here are the facts: Expenditures by the Mayor's Office were budgeted for, submitted, and subject to annual audit during my twelve years delivering results in a deep blue city, going from a $30 million deficit to a $34 million surplus."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/98cd7129-3237-4142-b59a-1c753dbe818d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Republican Gubernatorial Candidate Erin Stewart

But she did not deny the Courant's accusations. And prediction markets quickly flipped from favoring Stewart to be the Republican nominee to favor her main opponent, Ryan Fazio.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/94b6b798-10c3-41dc-860f-bf820402bb7b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

But does anyone in their right mind think that the Democrats running cities such as Waterbury, Bridgeport and Hartford aren't doing the same thing? Are we soon going to see a report in the Hartford Courant going over the personal expenses of the officials in these cities? If anyone thinks so, please send me a check for $500 and I will send you the title to the Verrazano Bridge.
Governor Ned Lamont - the great champion of the environment and fearless fighter against climate change - chopped down two hundred trees near his sumptuous Greenwich abode to get a better view of a pond. What happened to him? Absolutely nothing. And then a [no bid contract for COVID](https://substack.com/redirect/d501f18f-4777-4b55-9c52-f4e4d56db2b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) tests was rewarded to SEMA, a company in which Lamont's wife has partial ownership. What does the media and Attorney General Tong say? Nothing to see here.
And Democratic corruption is so common that Connecticut is now call Corrupticut with AG Tong ignoring blatant fraud while continuous filing frivolous lawsuits against the Trump administration to mollify bored Trump-hating former hippies. Meanwhile:
Wanda Geter-Pataky and her cohorts were caught on video committing ballot fraud in Bridgeport (Why am I not surprised?) with absentee ballots. They are about to get a slap on the wrist. In fact, the Democratic response to this was to simply pass a law making [absentee ballot fraud legal](https://substack.com/redirect/d21c1022-52a3-49f8-99f3-6d3129adf9dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
State Senator McCrory of Hartford (another paragon of good government) has been implicated in $300,000 of wired fraud through a "non profit" organization he controls, The Blue Hills Civic Association. The FBI is investigating. Don't hold your breath. But Governor Lamont swung the hatchet and demanded McCrory give up his leadership position in the Senate. Such suffering.
Terrence Cheng, former Chancellor of the Connecticut State Colleges and Universities managed to get himself a no-work job as a "special adviser" in which in pulled in $442,000 a year. AG Tong will be right on this no doubt.

Diedre Gifford who ran the Office of Healthcare Strategy (I have no idea what this is, but I am sure it pays well) [covered up Medicaid fraud](https://substack.com/redirect/04c3285a-9080-4b89-9ae5-377f5b3f15dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and had to resign. Charges? Nah.
I could go on but unfortunately my Word program does not have enough gigabytes to handle the volume.
But I should mention what happened to former Governor John Rowland. He was found guilty of having a state contractor do $8,000 work on his house for no charge. The result, eight months in jail. Once out, he was caught receiving money under the table to help a Congressional candidate. The result, t[hirty more months](https://substack.com/redirect/1eb77ed2-4ada-49e9-9faa-66e9f8a963c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in jail.

But Rowland's punishment far exceeded what was fair for his crimes, because his real crime was being a successful Republican.

And that is Erin Stewart's real crime. This moderate Republican could have returned the billionaire Lamont (funny how the Democrats and media never point this out) to his Greenwich abode where he could have spent quality time mastering the nuances of the various vintages of Chateau Lafite Rothschild. He may have even been able to figure out that 2017 was a bad year.

But Stewart is finding out what happens when the powers-that-be and their media toadies are challenged in the Peoples Republic of Corrupticut.

Derek –
This is a long but important email about the fight to level the playing field in Virginia and stop President Trump’s power grab. I hope you’ll take a moment to read it, but if you’re short on time and already with me and Tim Kaine in the fight to flip control of Congress, then please split a donation to our campaigns via the link below:
secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2026-warner [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2026-warner?amount=25]
The Virginia Supreme Court just ruled with Republicans to overturn a free and fair referendum to redraw congressional districts in Virginia.
So let's start with this: This is a major setback, but Virginia remains at the center of Democrats’ path towards flipping Congress.
Virginia’s redistricting fight started because Republicans across the country decided to push mid-decade redistricting in states where they thought they could rig the map for partisan gain. Virginia’s effort was a response to that national power grab, not the cause of it.
Donald Trump assumed he could tilt the playing field and lock in political advantage before a single ballot was cast.
Make no mistake: This decision is a huge victory for President Trump. The fight to flip control of Congress will not be easy, but it never was going to be.
And our work remains the same:
We will organize in every corner of Virginia. We will flood the airwaves with our message. We will make sure every Virginia voter knows exactly who ripped away their health care to give tax breaks to those at the very top, jeopardized their rural hospitals, and raised prices at the gas pump.
In fact, I’ve looked at the numbers – and I firmly believe there is still a path for Democrats to flip multiple Congressional seats in Virginia this year. I’m determined to campaign just as hard for those districts as I will for my race.
But that takes resources.
I consulted with my team, and we have decided to raise our fundraising goal for the month, so we can ensure Democrats have the resources they need to win big at the ballot box in November. Will you split a donation between Tim Kaine and me to help reach our important goal? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2026-warner?amount=25]
If you’ve saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:

We cannot be demoralized into inaction. We’ve got to stay in this fight. And we’ve got to kick butt at the ballot box this year.
The fight continues,
Mark
